items.title: Modalities and dosage of exercise interventions for improving adolescent mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

ai.headline: Exercise can reduce depression, anxiety and stress in adolescents, with specific types and doses showing promise.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at 17 randomised controlled trials of exercise interventions for adolescent mental health. Exercise significantly improved depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups; low-intensity TCC under three times a week for over 60 minutes, moderate-to-high-intensity HIIT over 60 minutes under three times a week, and low-intensity yoga for 30-60 minutes under three times a week were highlighted for different outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that regular physical activity may be a useful non-drug way to support teenage mental wellbeing alongside other support.
ai.life_skill: Try doing a gentle activity such as yoga or tai chi for 30-60 minutes a couple of times a week if you are feeling stressed.
ai.fact: Exercise interventions were linked to significant reductions in depression, anxiety and stress in adolescents in the included trials.

quiz.question: What did the review find about exercise and adolescent mental health?
quiz.answer: Exercise was linked to significant improvements in depression, anxiety and stress compared with control groups.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on only 17 trials with imbalanced subgroup sizes, and publication bias cannot be ruled out, so the specific exercise recommendations should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Decision for hysterectomy as a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Hysterectomy is linked to higher risks of high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity and metabolic syndrome.
ai.summary: This systematic review combined 20 studies looking at women who had a hysterectomy. It found the procedure was associated with increased risk of several cardiovascular risk factors, including hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity and metabolic syndrome.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests women who have had a hysterectomy may benefit from ongoing heart-health checks and follow-up.
ai.life_skill: If you have had a hysterectomy, ask a qualified health professional about regular blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol checks.
ai.fact: Hysterectomy is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity and metabolic syndrome.

quiz.question: What did the review find about hysterectomy and cardiovascular risk factors?
quiz.answer: Hysterectomy was associated with significantly increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity and metabolic syndrome.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and includes observational studies, so it shows links rather than proving hysterectomy causes these conditions.

items.title: Environmental Exposures and Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging Phenotypes in Cognitively Healthy Ageing: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: Air pollution is linked to differences in brain structure in healthy older adults, while greenspace may be linked to healthier brains.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 27 studies involving more than 84,000 older adults across 10 countries looked at environmental exposures and brain MRI scans. Higher exposure to air pollution, especially PM2.5, NO2, and PM10, was linked to smaller brain volumes and other structural changes, while greenspace was linked to more favourable brain structure in several studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that the air we breathe and the green spaces around us may be linked to brain health as we age, which could inform public policy.
ai.life_skill: Notice how much time you spend near busy roads versus in parks or green spaces.
ai.fact: Higher air pollution exposure was linked to smaller total, grey matter, and white matter brain volumes in cognitively healthy older adults.

quiz.question: What did the review find about air pollution and brain structure in healthy older adults?
quiz.answer: Higher air pollution exposure was associated with altered brain structure, including smaller brain volumes.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and most included studies were cross-sectional, so they show links rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: factors associated with stigma among adults with head and neck cancer: a systematic review

ai.headline: Stigma in head and neck cancer is linked to body image, distress, poorer physical function and lower self-efficacy.
ai.summary: A systematic review of eleven studies looked at factors linked to stigma among adults with head and neck cancer. Stigma was most consistently associated with body image disturbance, depression and anxiety, poorer physical functioning and lower self-efficacy, and was also linked to poorer quality of life.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how visible physical changes from illness can affect how people feel about themselves and their social lives.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in appearance or speech affect your confidence and speak to a healthcare professional if stigma or low mood is troubling you.
ai.fact: Stigma in head and neck cancer is linked to poorer quality of life and may be modifiable through intervention.

quiz.question: Which factors were most consistently linked to stigma in adults with head and neck cancer?
quiz.answer: Body image disturbance, psychological distress such as depression and anxiety, poorer physical functioning and lower self-efficacy.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were cross-sectional, so they show links rather than prove what causes stigma.

items.title: Editorial: Exploring the link between infectious diseases and mental health
items.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

ai.headline: Research links infections and immune responses to mental-health symptoms such as brain fog, fear, anxiety and depression.
ai.summary: The editorial reviews several studies on infections and mental health. It reports links between post-COVID cognitive complaints and test performance, pre-existing brain volume and fear during the pandemic, and recurrent urinary tract infections with anxiety or depression, while noting that some proposed links remain unproven.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that physical illness and mental symptoms can be connected, so 'brain fog' or low mood after infection may deserve attention rather than being dismissed.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether mood or thinking changes after an infection and discuss persistent changes with a qualified health professional.
ai.fact: Headache, muscle pain and fatigue or weakness were reported in about one quarter of people with mpox without HIV coinfection.

quiz.question: What did Watson et al. find about subjective cognitive complaints in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome?
quiz.answer: They were more closely related to objective neuropsychological performance than to fatigue, depression, or measured inflammatory cytokines.

ai.caveat: This is an editorial summarising multiple studies of different designs, so it is not itself proof of any single finding.

items.title: Diet Quality Versus Physical Activity and Cardiorespiratory Fitness for Longevity: A Review of Comparative Evidence.

ai.headline: Physical activity and fitness may matter more than diet quality for reducing early death risk.
ai.summary: The review compared diet quality, physical activity, and cardiorespiratory fitness against all-cause mortality using meta-analyses and cohort studies. It found that inactivity is linked to substantially greater excess mortality risk than poor diet, and that higher activity or fitness is linked to lower mortality risk than better diet quality alone.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that staying active and fit may be at least as important as eating well for living longer and avoiding chronic disease.
ai.life_skill: Try to move more regularly and improve your fitness alongside eating a healthy diet.
ai.fact: A sedentary lifestyle is linked to substantially greater excess mortality risk than poor diet quality.

quiz.question: According to the review, which is linked to substantially greater excess mortality risk: a sedentary lifestyle or poor diet quality?
quiz.answer: A sedentary lifestyle is linked to substantially greater excess mortality risk than poor diet quality.

ai.caveat: The evidence is largely observational, so it shows links rather than proving that activity or fitness directly causes lower mortality.

items.title: From Echo Chambers to Echo Machines? Endorsement, Evidence, and the Certainty of Belief in Conversations With AI

ai.headline: AI approval can make beliefs more certain even when the facts stay the same.
ai.summary: The paper reviews trials showing AI conversations can reduce conspiracy beliefs and political polarization, but also notes AI can increase conspiracy belief when instructed to. It proposes that social endorsement from an AI, separate from factual evidence, may increase certainty in a belief, potentially making it more rigid without changing its position.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that how an AI responds to you may affect how strongly you hold a belief, not just what you believe.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether an AI’s praise or agreement is changing how certain you feel about a claim.
ai.fact: Randomized trials show conversations with large language models can reduce conspiracy belief and modestly reduce political polarization.

quiz.question: What does the paper suggest AI endorsement might do to a belief without changing its factual content?
quiz.answer: It may increase the certainty with which the belief is held, making it more rigid.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that proposes a theory and experiments; the effects have not yet been tested in the studies described.

items.title: Effects of a mindfulness intervention on pre-competition mental states in youth athletes: a randomized controlled trial

ai.headline: An 8-week mindfulness programme reduced anxiety and improved sleep and resilience in young athletes.
ai.summary: A randomized trial assigned 120 adolescent athletes to either an 8-week mindfulness programme or an active sport-psychology education control. The mindfulness group showed significant improvements in anxiety, sleep quality and psychological resilience after the programme, while the control group did not; gains were still present four weeks later.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a simple, structured mindfulness routine may help young people manage stress-related states before competition or other high-pressure events.
ai.life_skill: Try a short daily mindfulness practice for several weeks if you want to feel calmer before a big event.
ai.fact: In this trial, athletes with higher baseline anxiety gained more in sleep quality and resilience from the mindfulness programme.

quiz.question: Did the control group show significant changes in anxiety, sleep quality or resilience?
quiz.answer: No, the control group showed no significant changes in these outcomes.

ai.caveat: The mediation analysis assessed the mediator and outcomes at the same time point, so it cannot prove that mindfulness caused the improvements.

items.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents

ai.headline: An AI model that makes poor choices can still be a good teacher by judging actions after seeing their results.
ai.summary: Researchers compared six AI models as actors and judges on two task websites. All models struggled to act because they were distracted by easier subgoals, but as judges they could credit useful steps, and using one model as a teacher improved a smaller policy’s success rates.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that judging something after the fact can be easier than doing it in the moment, which matters for how we learn from mistakes and train AI helpers.
ai.life_skill: Try reviewing what you did after a task to spot which steps actually helped, rather than only judging the final result.
ai.fact: Judging each action by whether it helped, rather than whether the whole task succeeded, can separate useful from useless actions.

quiz.question: What did the researchers find about models that acted poorly?
quiz.answer: They could still judge actions well and teach a policy to improve its success rates.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from AI experiments on two specific task websites rather than real people.

items.title: Development and validation of an explainable artificial intelligence model to predict in-hospital adverse events for patients with acute myocardial infarction

ai.headline: AI models can predict serious in-hospital complications after a heart attack using routine admission data.
ai.summary: Researchers developed and tested machine-learning models to predict atrial fibrillation, ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest, or death after acute myocardial infarction. XGBoost performed best, with moderate-to-good accuracy for atrial fibrillation and death, though predictions were weaker for ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how routinely collected hospital data might help clinicians spot higher-risk heart-attack patients earlier and target monitoring and treatment.
ai.life_skill: If you or someone you know is admitted after a heart attack, ask the care team how risk is being assessed and what monitoring is planned.
ai.fact: Neutrophil and leukocyte counts, NT-proBNP, kidney function, glucose, HbA1c, and prior atrial fibrillation were highlighted as important predictors.

quiz.question: Which model performed best for predicting the composite adverse outcome in the development cohort?
quiz.answer: XGBoost achieved the best performance, with an AUROC of 0.798.

ai.caveat: This was a retrospective observational study using existing records, so it shows associations rather than proving the models improve patient outcomes.

items.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction

ai.headline: A new AI model can see, hear and respond to users in real time without needing a mouse or keyboard.
ai.summary: The paper introduces Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. It combines two capabilities: Intent for reasoning and decision-making, and Realization for generating coherent audio-visual behavior. Users can interact through spontaneous conversation, interruptions, shared real objects, virtual scenes and audiovisual games.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI assistants might one day join everyday conversations and tasks naturally, without screens or keyboards.
ai.life_skill: Notice when an AI tool responds in real time and decide whether you trust it before sharing personal information.
ai.fact: Duo v1 is a preprint research model, not yet peer reviewed, so its real-world performance is not yet independently confirmed.

quiz.question: What does Duo v1 do continuously while interacting with users?
quiz.answer: It continuously perceives real-time audio, video and text while responding to users.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, so the claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Replicative and chronological epigenetic age track genome instability in opposite directions across cancers

ai.headline: Two types of epigenetic clock measure different things in cancer tissue.
ai.summary: Researchers compared mitotic clocks, which count cell divisions, with Horvath’s chronological clock across 506 adult and 1,731 pediatric tumor samples. Mitotic age was higher in tumors than matched normal tissue in every adult cancer type, while Horvath age varied by cancer type and was often younger in children’s tumors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that epigenetic age readings in tumors are not a single measure of biological aging and should not be interpreted without knowing which clock was used.
ai.fact: Mitotic epigenetic age is near uniformly advanced across adult cancers, whereas Horvath clock readings vary by cancer type.

quiz.question: What did the study find about mitotic age in adult tumors compared with matched normal tissue?
quiz.answer: Mitotic age was higher in the tumor than in matched normal tissue in every adult cancer type.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are preliminary.

items.title: What is 'food is medicine'? Two experts explain this decades‑old approach to health care that is taking on new life

ai.headline: A healthy diet can help manage chronic conditions such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.
ai.summary: The article explains the 'food is medicine' approach to healthcare. It notes that research shows eating habits affect health, and a healthy diet can help people with chronic conditions like type 2 diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday food choices can support the management of common long-term health conditions.
ai.life_skill: Try eating a balanced, healthy diet to support your overall health.
ai.fact: A healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like type 2 diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.

quiz.question: Which chronic conditions can a healthy diet help with, according to the article?
quiz.answer: A healthy diet can help those suffering from type 2 diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.

ai.caveat: This is a news article summarising expert views rather than a peer-reviewed study, so it does not provide specific evidence or proof.

items.title: Bird flu: Fear of ICE may discourage dairy workers from seeking testing, US union warns

ai.headline: Fear of immigration enforcement may stop dairy workers getting bird flu tests, hiding infections.
ai.summary: A US farm workers' union says dairy workers in Washington state with bird flu symptoms are avoiding testing because they fear immigration enforcement. Official figures show three human infections and one death in Yakima County, but the union believes many more cases are undiagnosed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how fear of authorities can block public health checks and let infections spread unnoticed.
ai.life_skill: Check trusted local health services for confidential testing options if you have flu-like symptoms after farm work.
ai.fact: Three human bird flu infections, including one death, have been confirmed in Yakima County, Washington.

quiz.question: Why might some dairy workers with bird flu symptoms not get tested?
quiz.answer: They fear immigration enforcement or other repercussions.

ai.caveat: This is a news report quoting a union warning, not a peer-reviewed study, so the scale of undercounting is not proven.

items.title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury

ai.headline: Scientists induced a hibernation-like state in rats that reduced heart attack damage by about 40%.
ai.summary: Researchers used a viral vector to activate a brain region in rats, creating a synthetic torpor state. In an isolated heart model, this state reduced infarct size by around 40% without needing prior cooling, and protein analysis suggests it activates survival pathways while blocking cell death.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how a hibernation-like brain state might one day protect the heart from damage during events like a heart attack.
ai.fact: Synthetic torpor reduced infarct size by approximately 40% in an ex vivo rat heart model.

quiz.question: What happened to infarct size when synthetic torpor was induced in rats?
quiz.answer: It was reduced by around 40%.

ai.caveat: This was an animal study using isolated rat hearts, so it cannot yet be applied to humans.

items.title: Trusted online information may help networking skills translate into startup ambitions, survey suggests

ai.headline: Trustworthy online networks and resources may help students turn entrepreneurial skills into business plans.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed nearly 200 undergraduate and postgraduate students in South Korea. They found that entrepreneurial skills were more likely to lead to startup intentions when students had access to trusted digital networks and useful online resources.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how online support can shape whether people act on their business ideas.
ai.life_skill: Look for reliable online networks and resources if you are thinking about starting a business.
ai.fact: Trustworthy digital networks and useful online resources are linked to stronger startup intentions among students with entrepreneurial skills.

quiz.question: What did the study find about entrepreneurial skills and startup plans?
quiz.answer: They were more likely to translate into startup intentions when supported by trustworthy digital networks and useful online resources.

ai.caveat: It is a single survey-based observational study, so it cannot show that online support causes stronger startup intentions.

items.title: Gut and urogenital microbiomes influence menopausal hormone therapy outcomes

ai.headline: Your gut and vaginal bacteria may influence how well menopausal hormone therapy works.
ai.summary: A six-month study found that menopausal hormone therapy changes the bacteria in the gut and vagina, making the vaginal community look more like that of a younger woman. The types of bacteria present before starting treatment were linked to how well the therapy worked for symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: This suggests that individual differences in body bacteria could help doctors predict who will benefit most from hormone therapy, moving towards more personalised care.
ai.life_skill: Mention your gut health or any unusual symptoms to your doctor when discussing hormone therapy options.
ai.fact: Menopausal hormone therapy is linked to a 'rejuvenation' of the vaginal microbiome, shifting it toward a state typical of reproductive age.

quiz.question: What did the study find about the vaginal microbiome after hormone therapy?
quiz.answer: The vaginal microbial community shifted toward a state similar to that of a woman of reproductive age.

ai.caveat: This was a six-month observational study, so it shows links between bacteria and treatment response but does not prove that changing the bacteria causes better outcomes.

items.title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method

ai.headline: A new obesity diagnosis using waist size predicts health risks better than BMI alone.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a 2025 framework that uses waist circumference and organ function to diagnose obesity. In a study of over 844,000 adults, this method outperformed standard BMI criteria for identifying obesity and predicting mortality risk.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that where you carry weight and how it affects your organs matters more for health than your weight on the scale alone.
ai.life_skill: Notice that health assessments often consider body shape and organ function, not just weight.
ai.fact: A framework incorporating waist circumference and organ dysfunction distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity.

quiz.question: What did the new framework use that BMI does not?
quiz.answer: It incorporated waist circumference and measures of obesity-induced organ dysfunction.

ai.caveat: This is an observational study, so it shows a link between the diagnostic method and risk, but does not prove the method causes better health outcomes.

items.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

ai.headline: AI helps predict light patterns seen by a blind person with a brain implant.
ai.summary: Researchers tested an AI method with an experimental brain implant in a blind man. The AI learned how his brain responded to electrical stimulation and predicted the flashes and shapes of light he perceived. This suggests the approach could make bionic vision more precise.

ai.headline: High-intensity inspiratory muscle training may lower blood pressure in healthy adults, but evidence is limited.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at six studies involving 134 mostly young men with normal blood pressure. It found that six weeks of high-intensity inspiratory muscle training reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure, while lower-intensity training did not change blood pressure.

ai.summary: A scoping review of 14 studies looked at first responders exposed to traumatic events through disaster work or routine jobs. ai.summary: This obituary highlights the work of Nobel prizewinner Hideki Shirakawa, who discovered that plastics could conduct electricity. This finding led to the development of new materials, light-emitting diodes, and solar cells.

items.title: Yvette Cooper unveils new NHS quango as part of abolishing “world’s largest quango”

ai.headline: The UK government is replacing NHS England with a new NHS body separate from the Department of Health and Social Care.
ai.summary: The government announced it would abolish NHS England, described as “the world’s largest quango,” to remove what it called two layers of bureaucracy. The health secretary has now confirmed a new NHS body separate from DHSC will take on NHS England’s regional work, while most national delivery functions will transfer elsewhere. The change has faced reported problems, including pay discrepancies for staff moving into the civil service and large redundancy costs.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how major public services are reorganised and why such changes can be costly and difficult to carry out.

items.title: Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke

ai.headline: A large US study links even occasional cannabis use to higher reported odds of stroke.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed data from over 440,000 Americans to examine the relationship between cannabis use and cardiovascular health. They found that people who used marijuana occasionally reported 40% higher odds of having a history of stroke compared to non-users.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that even infrequent use of substances may carry health risks that are not immediately obvious to the user.
ai.life_skill: Check whether your occasional habits might have long-term health consequences you have not considered.
ai.fact: The study found a link between occasional cannabis use and a higher reported history of stroke.

quiz.question: Did the study prove that cannabis directly causes strokes?
quiz.answer: No, the researchers have not established that cannabis directly causes strokes or heart disease.

ai.caveat: This is an observational study, so it shows a link but cannot prove that cannabis causes stroke.

items.title: Microplastics found in wild mammals' blood more than 40 miles from human infrastructure

ai.headline: Wild mammals far from human areas have microplastics in their blood, confirming a link to environmental exposure.
ai.summary: Researchers studied wild mammals living more than 40 miles from human infrastructure to check if environmental plastic levels affect their bodies. They found that higher exposure to microplastics in the environment is linked to higher accumulation of these particles in the animals' blood.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that plastic pollution reaches even remote wild areas and enters the bodies of animals, highlighting the widespread impact of human waste on nature.
ai.life_skill: Notice how much single-use plastic you use and consider reducing it to help lower overall pollution.
ai.fact: Microplastics have been detected in the blood of wild mammals living far from human settlements.

quiz.question: What did the study find about the relationship between environmental exposure and microplastics in animals?
quiz.answer: Higher exposure to microplastics in the environment is linked to higher accumulation in the animals' blood.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising a study, and while it confirms a link, it does not prove that microplastics cause specific health problems in these wild animals.

items.title: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts

ai.headline: Ancient parchment holds DNA from a deadly sheep virus unchanged for thousands of years.
ai.summary: Scientists studied 1,000-year-old manuscripts, including the York Gospels, and found traces of a deadly sheep virus. The virus has remained remarkably unchanged for more than 3,700 years, making old parchment an unexpected record of ancient disease.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how old documents can help us understand how diseases have persisted and changed over thousands of years.
ai.life_skill: Try thinking of everyday objects, like old books, as possible records of history and science.
ai.fact: A deadly sheep virus has a history stretching back more than 3,700 years.

quiz.question: What did scientists find in 1,000-year-old manuscripts?
quiz.answer: Traces of a deadly sheep virus that has remained remarkably unchanged for more than 3,700 years.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original peer-reviewed research, so details and conclusions should be checked against the full study.

ai.why_it_matters: It raises a question about who will safeguard important historical objects from the space age and why that matters for future generations.

quiz.answer: They were linked to death from H7N7 avian influenza.

items.title: Exploring Changes in Students’ Subjective Sleep Quality, Sleep Beliefs, and Pre-Sleep Arousal After Attending a Curriculum-Embedded University Course on Sleep

ai.headline: A university sleep course was linked to better sleep quality and fewer unhelpful sleep beliefs in students.
ai.summary: Seventy-five students completed questionnaires before and after a three-month course, either on sleep psychology or history of psychology. Those on the sleep course showed improvements in subjective sleep quality, sleep disturbances, pre-sleep cognitive arousal, and some sleep beliefs compared with the comparison course.
ai.why_it_matters: Learning about sleep may help students develop healthier sleep habits and thinking patterns.
ai.life_skill: Try learning more about how sleep works and what affects it.
ai.fact: The study found changes in subjective sleep quality, sleep disturbances, cognitive arousal and sleep beliefs among students who took a sleep course.

quiz.question: What did students who took the sleep psychology course show compared with those who took history of psychology?
quiz.answer: They showed greater improvements in subjective sleep quality, sleep disturbances, pre-sleep cognitive arousal and some sleep beliefs.

ai.caveat: This was a small non-randomised exploratory study, so the results cannot prove the sleep course caused the changes.

items.title: Machine Learning Models for Glycemic Prediction in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

ai.headline: Machine-learning tools can forecast blood sugar in diabetes, but most studies are too biased to trust yet.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 270 studies on machine-learning models that predict future blood sugar levels in people with type 1, type 2, or mixed diabetes. The pooled results suggested reasonable forecasting accuracy, but nearly all studies had a high risk of bias, and very few were externally or prospectively validated.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI-based blood-sugar prediction is promising but not yet reliable enough for everyday use without stronger evidence.
ai.fact: Only 4% of the 270 studies externally validated their machine-learning models.

quiz.question: What did the review find about external validation in the 270 studies?
quiz.answer: External validation occurred in only 4% of studies.

ai.caveat: Most included studies had a high risk of bias and few were externally or prospectively validated, so the pooled estimates are not yet deployable benchmarks.

items.title: The gender pay gap during conflict: evidence from farm workers in Myanmar

ai.headline: In Myanmar’s conflict zones, women farm workers earn 19% less than men due to structural inequality, not personal traits.
ai.summary: The study looked at 1,504 hired farm workers across Myanmar during conflict after the 2021 military coup. It found a 19% gender pay gap driven by structural inequalities rather than individual characteristics, and that the gap stayed the same even in areas with more fighting.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how conflict can lock in unfair pay for women in farming, affecting livelihoods and food security.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether pay differences at work are based on the job itself rather than who is doing it.
ai.fact: A 19% gender pay gap among hired farm workers in Myanmar is linked to structural inequalities rather than individual traits.

quiz.question: What did the study find drives the 19% gender pay gap among farm workers in Myanmar?
quiz.answer: The gap is driven by structural inequalities rather than individual traits.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study from one country, so it shows a link rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Do what you want to do: an analysis of positive mental health literacy among pre-service teachers at a regional university in China

ai.headline: Pre-service teachers in China show generally high positive mental health literacy, linked to motivation and study year.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 455 pre-service teachers at one university in Hunan Province using questionnaires and open questions. They found generally high positive mental health literacy, with differences linked to year of study, gender and career motivation, while employment pressure was a common stressor and leisure, social support and goals were seen as supports.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how motivation and everyday supports may relate to wellbeing among people training to be teachers.
ai.life_skill: Notice what activities, people and goals help you feel mentally well, especially when facing study or work pressure.
ai.fact: Positive mental health literacy is described as a resource for promoting psychological wellbeing and resilience.

quiz.question: What did the study find about differences in positive mental health literacy among pre-service teachers?
quiz.answer: Differences were linked to year of study, gender and career motivation, with career motivation showing the largest association.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study at one university, so it shows links rather than causes and may not apply to all pre-service teachers in China.

items.title: Quantifying Academic Risk Factors for Student Depression Using WHO Frameworks: Odds Ratios, SHAP Explainability, and Tipping Point Analysis

ai.headline: High academic pressure is linked to student depression, while more sleep and study satisfaction may protect against it.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed data from 27,880 university students in India to see how five academic factors relate to depression. Academic pressure was the strongest risk factor, while longer sleep duration and higher study satisfaction were linked to lower odds of depression.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which everyday student experiences are linked to depression risk, helping schools and students spot warning signs early.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your academic pressure, sleep, and study satisfaction are affecting your mood, and consider speaking with a counsellor if they are.
ai.fact: Academic pressure, work/study hours, study satisfaction, sleep duration, and financial stress are academically relevant factors linked to student depression.

quiz.question: Which factor was the strongest risk factor for depression in this study?
quiz.answer: Academic pressure was the dominant risk factor.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and as an observational study it cannot prove that academic pressure causes depression.

items.title: Multiple Methods for Visualizing Human Language: A Tutorial for Social and Behavioural Scientists

ai.headline: Researchers can use visual tools to show how language links to psychological states like well-being and mental health.
ai.summary: This tutorial explains how social and behavioural scientists can turn language data into visual insights using R packages. It covers four ways to visualize language: individual words and phrases, word clusters called topics, words in an embedding space, and relevant language examples. These visualizations help interpret assessment scores, uncover patterns, and explain links between language use and mental states.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday language can be studied to better understand psychological experiences such as well-being and mental health.
ai.life_skill: Notice how the words you use might reflect your mood or state of mind.
ai.fact: Natural Language Processing lets researchers quantitatively study psychological states and behaviors through language.

quiz.question: What are the four types of language visualizations described in the tutorial?
quiz.answer: Individual words and phrases, topics, words in the word embedding space, and relevant language examples.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint tutorial, not peer-reviewed research, so its methods have not yet been independently validated.

items.title: Addressing barriers and facilitators to family planning uptake among adolescent girls and young women in the anticipated context of long-acting antiretroviral therapy (LA ART)

ai.headline: Young women living with HIV face policy, health system, peer and personal barriers to family planning access.
ai.summary: Researchers held focus groups with 58 adolescents, young people living with HIV, healthcare providers, advocates and policymakers in western Kenya. They found barriers such as parental consent rules, provider stigma, inadequate youth-friendly services, supply gaps, peer misinformation, parental disapproval, myths and fear of side effects, while discreet low-maintenance contraceptives were preferred.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how family planning services could be better integrated with HIV care to support young women’s reproductive choices.
ai.life_skill: Check whether local sexual health services offer youth-friendly, confidential contraceptive advice and long-acting options.
ai.fact: Adolescent girls and young women aged 15–24 bear a disproportionate global HIV burden, with nearly twice as many living with HIV as adolescent boys and young men.

quiz.question: What did participants say influenced contraceptive choices at the individual level?
quiz.answer: Adolescents preferred discreet, low-maintenance methods, though myths, side effect fears and procedural anxiety influenced choices.

ai.caveat: The findings come from focus groups in one Kenyan clinic and cannot be generalised to all settings or prove cause and effect.

items.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents

ai.headline: AI agents can improve chip design by rewriting code and tuning synthesis tools.
ai.summary: The paper studies autonomous agents for hardware design optimization. It introduces Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that analyses critical paths, rewrites RTL code, and improves itself through reusable skills. On 20 real-world designs, it achieved average WNS/TNS improvements of 21%/17% and a 6% area reduction over commercial synthesis.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could speed up and improve the design of the chips inside everyday electronics.
ai.life_skill: Notice how AI agents can break complex tasks into smaller steps and improve by reusing what worked before.
ai.fact: Dr. RTL achieved average WNS/TNS improvements of 21%/17% with a 6% area reduction over commercial synthesis on 20 real-world RTL designs.

quiz.question: What did Dr. RTL achieve on 20 real-world RTL designs compared with commercial synthesis?
quiz.answer: It achieved average WNS/TNS improvements of 21%/17% with a 6% area reduction.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the results come from a specific framework evaluated on a limited set of designs.

items.title: Shared experimental materials inflate and reorder cross-participant decoding benchmarks

ai.headline: Brain-decoding benchmarks can look better than they are because everyone sees the same test materials.
ai.summary: Researchers compared how well brain-activity decoders generalise to new people across 15 EEG, fMRI and eye-tracking datasets. When test materials were shared across participants, accuracy was inflated by up to 46 percentage points and method rankings changed; the inflation disappeared when materials could not be identified across people.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that some widely used measures of mind-reading technology may overstate how well it works across different brains.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a brain-decoding result was tested on completely new materials before treating it as proof it generalises to new people.
ai.fact: Adding training items improved accuracy on new materials more reliably than adding more participants.

quiz.question: What happened to the inflation in decoding accuracy when test materials could not be identified across participants?
quiz.answer: It vanished in sealed prospective tests.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Evaluating the Parental Burnout Assessment in parents of children with and without complex care needs: Measurement invariance, group differences, and the correlates of sociodemographic characteristics

ai.headline: Parents of children with complex care needs report much higher parental burnout than other parents.
ai.summary: The study compared 337 parents of children with complex care needs and 329 parents without such children using the Parental Burnout Assessment. Parents of children with complex care needs scored significantly higher on burnout, and mothers in this group reported substantially higher scores than fathers.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that caring for a child with complex needs can place parents under greater emotional strain, which matters for recognising when support might be needed.
ai.life_skill: Notice signs of exhaustion or emotional distancing in yourself as a parent and consider speaking with a qualified professional if they persist.
ai.fact: Parents of children with complex care needs reported significantly higher parental burnout scores than parents of children without complex care needs.

quiz.question: Which group reported significantly higher parental burnout scores?
quiz.answer: Parents of children with complex care needs reported significantly higher scores than parents of children without complex care needs.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the cross-sectional design cannot show that complex care needs cause burnout.

items.title: Brain imaging uncovers a shared memory network linked to mild cognitive impairment

ai.summary: The study used brain imaging to look at memory problems in older adults. It found a shared brain network linked to mild cognitive impairment, including in people who report memory decline despite normal test scores.

items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz

ai.headline: Microplastics in Brazilian tapirs and anteaters increase with human land use, but remote animals are also affected.
ai.summary: The study looked at microplastic burdens in Brazilian tapirs and anteaters. It found that burdens rise with human-modified land use and proximity to development, yet animals in remote habitats also carry microplastics. Landscape change and individual space use together shape wildlife exposure.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that plastic pollution reaches wildlife even in remote areas, not just places near human development.
ai.life_skill: Notice how far plastic waste can travel and reduce single-use plastic where you can.
ai.fact: Microplastics have been found in wildlife living in remote habitats as well as in human-modified landscapes.

quiz.answer: Yes, animals in remote habitats also carry microplastics.

items.title: Outcomes of School-Based Mental Health Screening Programs: A Systematic Review

ai.headline: School mental health screening helps spot students who need support and increases service use, but effects on symptoms and grades are uncertain.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 22 studies of school-based mental health screening for children and adolescents aged 5–18. Screening consistently improved identification of mental health needs and was generally linked to greater use of mental health services, but effects on anxiety and depressive symptoms were inconsistent, and evidence on academic outcomes was limited and mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that schools can help find young people who might otherwise miss out on mental health support, though screening alone does not guarantee better symptoms or school results.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or a friend are struggling and speak to a trusted adult or school staff member so help can be arranged.
ai.fact: School-based screening is consistently linked to better identification of students with mental health needs and greater use of mental health services.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the effect of school-based screening on anxiety and depressive symptoms?
quiz.answer: Effects on anxiety and depressive symptoms were inconsistent, and several trials found no between-group difference.

ai.caveat: Study quality was not formally appraised and designs, screening tools, and outcome measures varied widely, so findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With Cancer and Their Parents and for Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults Affected by Parental Cancer: A Population-Stratified Systematic Review.

ai.headline: ACT may reduce distress and anxiety in parents of young people with cancer, but evidence for young people themselves is weak.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at nine studies involving 573 people to see if acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) helps children, adolescents, young adults with cancer, those affected by parental cancer, and their parents. It found moderate-certainty evidence that ACT reduced distress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms in parents, while evidence for young people was of very low certainty.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a specific talking therapy can support the mental health of parents caring for a young person with cancer, while highlighting that more research is needed for the young people themselves.
ai.life_skill: Notice when difficult thoughts or feelings show up and try to acknowledge them without judging yourself.
ai.fact: Psychological flexibility was identified as a possible factor behind quality-of-life improvements in one study of distressed adolescents and young adults affected by their own or a family member's cancer.

quiz.question: Which group showed moderate-certainty reductions in distress, anxiety, and depressive symptoms from ACT?
quiz.answer: Parents of children, adolescents, and young adults with cancer.

ai.caveat: The findings for young people are based on very low-certainty evidence and a mix of weak study designs, so they are not proof that ACT works for them.

items.title: Advancing a Global Framework for AI Safety and Governance for the Well-being of Humanity

ai.headline: Experts propose a UN-centered global framework to govern AI safety and promote human well-being.
ai.summary: The paper reviews current global approaches to AI safety and governance and identifies key issues such as safety, inclusiveness, accountability, coordination and effective governance. ai.why_it_matters: AI governance shapes how technology affects daily life, jobs, safety and fairness around the world.

ai.fact: The report calls for a United Nations-centered global AI safety and governance framework.

quiz.question: What kind of global AI governance framework does the report propose?
quiz.answer: A United Nations-centered framework based on multilateralism.

items.title: Effects of infertility on relationship quality and mental health outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review

ai.headline: Infertility is linked to poorer mental health and lower relationship quality in sub-Saharan Africa.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 70 studies looked at how infertility affects people in sub-Saharan Africa. It found infertility is linked to anxiety, depression, emotional distress, isolation, grief, and lower relationship quality, including abuse, infidelity, and separation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how social pressure around having children can affect relationships and mental wellbeing, highlighting the need for better support.
ai.life_skill: Notice if someone you know is struggling with infertility and offer non-judgmental support rather than pressure or blame.
ai.fact: Infertility is associated with anxiety, depression, emotional distress, isolation, and grief over unfulfilled reproductive goals.

quiz.question: What did the review find about infertility and relationship quality?
quiz.answer: Diminished relationship quality was common, including intimate partner violence, verbal and emotional abuse, loss of intimacy, infidelity, and separation or divorce.

ai.caveat: A scoping review maps existing evidence but does not prove cause and effect, and the included studies vary in design and quality.

items.title: Physical activity intervention for blood pressure reduction in low and middle-income countries: a systematic review with meta-analysis

ai.headline: Structured physical activity programmes lower blood pressure in adults with hypertension in low- and middle-income countries.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 45 studies of adults with high blood pressure in low- and middle-income countries who took part in physical activity programmes. Compared with control groups, office systolic blood pressure fell by about 10 mmHg and diastolic by about 5 mmHg, though effects varied across settings.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercise can be a practical way to help manage high blood pressure in many parts of the world.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular physical activity into your routine if you have high blood pressure, after checking with a health professional.
ai.fact: Physical activity interventions reduced office systolic blood pressure by an average of 10.23 mmHg compared with control in chronic controlled trials.

quiz.question: By how much did physical activity reduce office systolic blood pressure compared with control in chronic controlled trials?
quiz.answer: It reduced it by an average of 10.23 mmHg.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mainly from office blood pressure readings, with limited data on 24-hour ambulatory monitoring and long-term community programmes, and results varied across studies.

items.title: An impact assessment of a reading and writing instruction method in a socially vulnerable context

ai.headline: A Spanish early literacy program improved reading and writing skills in young children from vulnerable backgrounds.
ai.summary: The study tested the Sophia Method, which teaches linguistic, metalinguistic, and graphomotor skills, with 280 Uruguayan preschool and first-grade students from socioeconomically vulnerable schools. Children in the intervention group showed higher adjusted posttest performance across all three educational levels compared to a comparison group, with larger gains for some students who started with lower pretest scores.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how structured early literacy teaching can support children facing socioeconomic disadvantage.
ai.life_skill: Try practising letter sounds and writing letters regularly to build early reading skills.
ai.fact: The Sophia Method integrates explicit teaching of linguistic, metalinguistic, and graphomotor skills with systematic reading and writing instruction.

quiz.question: Did children in the intervention group perform better after the program than the comparison group?
quiz.answer: Yes, they showed higher adjusted posttest performance across all three educational levels.

ai.caveat: The study used a quasi-experimental design rather than random assignment, so it cannot prove the method caused the improvements.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Local-Level Food Environment Policies in Improving Diet Quality of Socioeconomically Disadvantaged Population Groups. A Systematic Literature Review.

ai.headline: Local food policies can modestly improve diet quality for disadvantaged groups, especially with financial incentives and combined approaches.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined 77 studies covering 104 local government food environment policies, mostly in US municipalities, aimed at improving diet quality among socioeconomically disadvantaged people. It found that effectiveness was generally modest or mixed, with economic incentives and combined environmental-behavioural approaches showing the most consistent benefits, while isolated infrastructure or labelling policies had limited impact.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how local rules about food shops, prices and provision can shape everyday eating, especially for people on low incomes.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether local food schemes offer financial incentives or combine several changes, as these are more likely to help improve diet quality.
ai.fact: Economic incentives and combined environmental-behavioural food policies produced the most consistent dietary gains among disadvantaged groups.
ai.caveat: The included studies had risk of bias, vague outcome evaluation, and resource constraints affecting sustainability, so findings should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.

items.title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns

ai.headline: A new computer method finds activity patterns linked to diseases using wearable tracker data.
ai.summary: Researchers developed LocPA, a framework that analyses 24-hour accelerometer data to find physical activity patterns enriched in specific diseases. Applied to UK Biobank data across six diseases, it found two common patterns: low daytime activity and disrupted sleep with elevated nighttime activity, with the latter linked to worse health in hypertension and diabetes.
