items.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling

ai.headline: A new computer benchmark tests whether AI agents can solve real-world maths modelling problems and check if answers are physically possible.
ai.summary: Researchers created TB-MathModel, a benchmark using 18 real contest-style maths problems where AI agents work in a terminal and return one JSON answer. The system scores answers against multiple outstanding human papers and uses a hard gate that zeroes answers that are not physically feasible, with top multimodal models reaching 64.58% and an open model reaching 59.81%.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how researchers are building ways to measure whether AI can turn messy real-world problems into workable mathematical solutions, which matters as these tools are used more in everyday decision-making.

quiz.question: What happens to an answer in TB-MathModel if it is not physically feasible?
quiz.answer: A hard gate zeroes infeasible answers.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet confirmed.

items.title: Rise of Germanic and Celtic languages is written in ancient DNA

ai.headline: Ancient DNA from thousands of genomes suggests migrations may have spread early Germanic and Celtic languages across Europe.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed thousands of genome sequences to trace human movements in Europe. Their findings suggest that migrations could have carried early forms of Germanic and Celtic languages across the continent.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how studying ancient DNA can help us understand how languages and people moved across Europe in the distant past.
ai.fact: Thousands of ancient genome sequences have been used to identify human migrations linked to the spread of early Germanic and Celtic languages.

quiz.question: What did researchers use thousands of genome sequences to identify?
quiz.answer: They used them to identify human migrations that might have spread early forms of Germanic and Celtic languages around Europe.

ai.caveat: The study identifies migrations that might have spread languages, but cannot prove that migration caused the languages to spread.

items.title: Parkinson’s may be driven by ‘vicious cycle’ that disrupts brain waste drainage

ai.headline: Parkinson’s may be driven by a cycle linking toxic protein clumps and poor brain waste drainage
ai.summary: The report discusses Parkinson’s disease, which is linked to toxic protein clumps and disrupted brain waste removal. It suggests these two problems may feed off each other, helping the condition progress.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights how brain waste clearance could be important in understanding how Parkinson’s develops and worsens over time.
ai.fact: Parkinson’s disease is linked to toxic protein clumps and disrupted brain waste removal.

quiz.question: What may feed off each other in Parkinson’s disease according to the report?
quiz.answer: Toxic protein clumps and disrupted brain waste removal may feed off each other.

ai.caveat: This is a news article summarising research, not the original study, so no methods or results can be verified from the abstract alone.

items.title: [Correspondence] Global health: dying from failure or fulfilment?

ai.headline: A Lancet editor reflects on whether global health has lost its radical edge and links it to citizen organising in Japan.
ai.summary: Richard Horton writes a letter to The Lancet asking if global health can recover its lost radicalism, referencing Saul Alinsky's Reveille for Radicals. He notes the book was translated into Japanese in 1972, arriving during a period of citizen movements against industrial pollution and other social problems in Japan.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how ideas about citizen participation and power can shape responses to health and social problems in different countries.
ai.life_skill: Notice how community groups organise around local problems and consider whether you could join or support one.
ai.fact: Saul Alinsky's Reveille for Radicals was translated into Japanese and published in 1972.

quiz.question: What does Richard Horton ask about global health in this letter?
quiz.answer: He asks whether global health can recover its lost radicalism.

ai.caveat: This is a short editorial letter offering opinion and historical context, not a research study with data.

items.title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial.

ai.headline: AI patient simulators may help medical students practise communication, but did not outperform conventional training in this trial.
ai.summary: A UK randomised trial followed 50 medical students for one academic year. Those using an AI-powered patient simulator improved descriptively more than controls, but the difference was not statistically significant; gains were linked to motivation and behavioural engagement.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that digital practice tools can support learning communication skills, but they are not yet proven to beat standard teaching.
ai.life_skill: Try practising difficult conversations regularly, whether with a person or a simulated tool, and notice what keeps you motivated to keep going.
ai.fact: In this trial, students’ communication skills improved over one academic year, and greater intrinsic motivation and behavioural learning were linked to larger gains.

quiz.question: Did the AI simulator group show a statistically significant improvement over conventional training?
quiz.answer: No, the AI group improved descriptively more, but the between-group difference was not statistically significant.

ai.caveat: The trial was small, non-blinded, and the AI-group advantage did not reach statistical significance, so the result should be treated as preliminary rather than proof.

items.title: Mental health of migrants in South Asia: a scoping review
items.venue: International Journal of Migration Health and Social Care

ai.headline: A review of 80 studies links migration in South Asia to depression, anxiety and PTSD, with trauma, poverty and isolation as key risks.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 80 peer-reviewed studies on migrant mental health in South Asia. Depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder were commonly studied, especially among refugees, displaced people and labour migrants. Violence, economic hardship, social isolation and discrimination were linked to poorer mental health, while family support, cultural practices and community resilience were protective.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how migration-related stress can affect mental wellbeing and highlights groups whose needs are often overlooked.
ai.life_skill: Notice if you or someone you know feels isolated or overwhelmed after moving, and consider reaching out to family, community or a qualified professional for support.
ai.fact: Family support, cultural practices and community resilience were identified as protective factors for migrant mental health in South Asia.

quiz.question: Which mental health issues were commonly studied among migrants in South Asia?
quiz.answer: Depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder were commonly studied.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were cross-sectional, so they show links rather than proving causes.

items.title: Context-driven mHealth solutions to improve maternal healthcare uptake in Ethiopia: Integrating stakeholder preferences and expert priorities using qualitative and nominal group techniques

ai.headline: Ethiopian women and experts agree on mobile health tools to improve maternal care uptake.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 72 perinatal women, male partners and key informants and held a workshop with 14 experts in Ethiopia. Participants preferred educational videos, text reminders followed by calls, involving spouses or support persons, and reminders sent between sunrise and midday the day before appointments.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mobile health services can be shaped around local preferences and practical barriers to help more women attend pregnancy and postnatal care.
ai.life_skill: Notice what practical barriers, such as device access or network coverage, might stop a digital service from working in your community.
ai.fact: Only about one-quarter of women in Ethiopia complete the full continuum of maternal healthcare.
ai.caveat: This is a small qualitative and consensus study in one setting, so its findings are not proof that these interventions will work everywhere or improve health outcomes.

items.title: A Multimodal Study of Screen Use in Adolescents Across Brain Structure, Social Media, and Gaming Use

ai.headline: Problematic social media and gaming use are more strongly linked to adolescent attention problems than hours of screen time alone.
ai.summary: Researchers looked at over 11,000 adolescents and compared screen time, problematic social media use and problematic gaming with parent-rated mental health and brain measures. Problematic use scales were more strongly related to attention problems than hours of use, and more screen time was linked to slightly smaller putamen and caudate volumes.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that how difficult a young person finds it to control their screen use may matter more for attention than the number of hours spent online.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you struggle to stop using social media or games, rather than only counting screen hours.
ai.fact: More screen time was associated with slightly smaller putamen and caudate volumes in adolescents.

quiz.question: Which was more strongly related to attention problems: hours of screen time or problematic use scales?
quiz.answer: The problematic social media and gaming use scales were more strongly related to attention problems than hours of use were.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings are observational so they cannot show that screen use causes attention problems or brain changes.

items.title: Spanish translation, cross-cultural adaptation, and psychometric validation of the CATQ-S and FATQ-S: assessing motivational functions of online and face-to-face aggression in secondary school students

ai.headline: Spanish questionnaires measuring why teenagers act aggressively online and face-to-face were validated for use in schools.
ai.summary: Researchers translated and culturally adapted two short questionnaires about the motivational functions of cyber and face-to-face aggression for Spanish secondary school students. Testing with 1,443 students aged 11–16 found the tools generally work well for boys and girls, though some aggression motives overlap too much to be clearly separated.
ai.why_it_matters: It gives schools and researchers a way to understand what drives peer aggression, which can inform efforts to support students’ wellbeing and safety.
ai.life_skill: Notice what might be driving aggressive behaviour—online or in person—before reacting.
ai.fact: The study involved 1,443 compulsory secondary education students from public schools in Extremadura, Spain.

quiz.question: What did the researchers validate for Spanish secondary school students?
quiz.answer: Short Spanish versions of questionnaires assessing motivational functions of cyber and face-to-face aggression.

ai.caveat: This was a single cross-sectional study in one Spanish region, so it shows the questionnaires work in that context but does not prove they reduce aggression or apply everywhere.

items.title: Latent profile analysis of ecological literacy among Turkish parents: associations with sociodemographic characteristics

ai.headline: Turkish parents’ ecological literacy awareness was modest overall, with education and family size linked to profile groups.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 543 parents in Türkiye about environmental values and everyday practices. Awareness scores were modest overall and did not differ by sociodemographic characteristics, but three distinct profiles emerged, with education level and number of children weakly linked to profile membership.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that parents’ environmental values may not match their everyday actions, which matters because parents shape children’s understanding of environmental issues.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your everyday habits match your stated environmental values.
ai.fact: Ecological literacy includes both environmental values and their expression in everyday practices.

quiz.question: Did total ecological literacy scores differ across sociodemographic characteristics?
quiz.answer: No, total scores did not differ significantly across any characteristic examined.

ai.caveat: It used a convenience sample and self-reported awareness, so the results cannot prove cause and effect or apply beyond this group of parents in Türkiye.

items.title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Nurse-led care may lower blood pressure in low- and middle-income countries, but results for staying in care vary widely.
ai.summary: The review looked at 11 studies involving over 19,000 adults with hypertension in primary care clinics across Africa and Asia. Most studies found nurse-led interventions reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure, while retention rates and medication adherence showed mixed or limited results.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how community health workers can help manage a common long-term condition where doctors are scarce.
ai.life_skill: If you have high blood pressure, ask your clinic whether a nurse-led support programme is available and keep attending your appointments.
ai.fact: High blood pressure affects more than 1.28 billion adults worldwide and is a leading preventable cause of heart disease and stroke.

quiz.question: What did most studies find about blood pressure after nurse-led interventions?
quiz.answer: Most studies reported a reduction in systolic and diastolic blood pressure after the intervention.

ai.caveat: The studies used different designs and measures, had high or unclear risk of bias in missing data, and blood pressure reductions should not be treated as a single pooled effect.

items.title: Dance-based exercise for healthy brain aging in older adults: integrating neuroplasticity, cognitive reserve, physical fitness, social engagement, and mental well-being

ai.headline: Dance-based exercise may support brain health in older adults by combining physical, mental, social and emotional activity.
ai.summary: This narrative review examined how dance-based exercise might support healthy brain aging in older adults. It found that dance may be linked to better cognitive functioning, especially executive abilities and attention, as well as improvements in balance, mobility and functional performance. Its social and enjoyable nature may also support psychological well-being, though evidence on loneliness is mixed.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how one enjoyable activity could combine several habits that help keep the brain and body resilient as people age.
ai.life_skill: Try joining a regular dance or movement class that includes music, steps and other people.
ai.fact: Dance-based exercise combines aerobic movement, motor coordination, cognitive involvement, social interaction and emotional expression.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the link between dance-based exercise and loneliness in older adults?
quiz.answer: The evidence specifically concerning loneliness remains mixed.

ai.caveat: It is a narrative review of hypothesis-generating mechanisms and varied existing studies, not a pooled trial, so it cannot prove dance causes these benefits or identify the best way to do it.

items.title: Keyora Skin Systems Nutrition - Collagen Tripeptides

ai.headline: Research reviews collagen tripeptides for skin but warns evidence varies by product and study quality.
ai.summary: The paper reviews a series of studies on oral hydrolyzed collagen tripeptides for skin nutrition, covering molecular identity, absorption, cell biology, and clinical outcomes such as hydration, elasticity, and wrinkles. Some randomised human studies reported improvements in selected skin measures, while systematic reviews found substantial heterogeneity, methodological limitations, and funding-related concerns.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people understand that collagen supplement claims should be judged product-by-product rather than assumed to work universally.
ai.life_skill: Check a supplement’s specific ingredient details and supporting evidence before assuming it will improve your skin.
ai.fact: Some randomised human investigations reported improvements in selected skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle outcomes after collagen peptide supplementation.

quiz.question: What do systematic reviews say about the evidence for collagen peptide skin benefits?
quiz.answer: They identify substantial heterogeneity, methodological limitations, funding-related concerns, and differences in evidence robustness.

ai.caveat: The paper is a research framework and commentary rather than a single new trial, and it stresses that evidence from individual preparations does not prove the complete product works.

items.title: Digital health technologies and measurable management outcomes in primary care: A systematic review, descriptive quantitative synthesis, and temporal sensitivity analysis

ai.headline: Digital tools are widely used in primary care management, but their effects are hard to compare across studies.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 172 studies on digital health technologies such as telemedicine, electronic health records and AI in primary care. Telemedicine and mobile health were the most studied, while patient or professional satisfaction and operating costs were the most common measures. Because studies used different indicators and methods, the authors could not pool the results into a single overall conclusion.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that digital health is growing in everyday healthcare, but we still need clearer, standard ways to tell whether it actually improves services.
ai.life_skill: Notice which digital tools your GP surgery uses and ask how they affect waiting times or costs.
ai.fact: Telemedicine/mHealth was the largest category of digital health technology studied in primary care management.

quiz.question: Why did the authors not carry out a formal meta-analysis?
quiz.answer: Because the studies were too different in their methods and indicators to combine their results.

ai.caveat: The review describes associations across varied studies rather than proving that digital tools cause better management outcomes, and risk of bias was only checked in a subsample of 40 studies.

items.title: Data-informed online teacher training to improve student engagement during the transition to high school: a cluster randomised trial

ai.headline: A data-informed online teacher training program did not improve student engagement in PE or maths during the move to secondary school.
ai.summary: Researchers used data to pick six teacher behaviours that best predicted student engagement, then trained teachers in 20 low-income schools using a 12-hour mostly online program. The trial found no improvement in engagement in any subject, and students did not say their teachers used the targeted behaviours more.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that picking targets from data does not guarantee a short online training will change what happens in classrooms or help students feel more engaged.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing which teacher actions actually help you feel more involved in a lesson, rather than assuming a training course will fix engagement.
ai.fact: The study screened 71 teacher behaviours from four motivational theories using data from 1,799 students before selecting six target behaviours per subject.

quiz.question: Did the teacher training program improve student engagement in PE or maths?
quiz.answer: No, the intervention did not improve engagement in any specification.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the positive physical activity finding rested on only four intervention schools and did not survive statistical correction.

items.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"

ai.headline: An AI reading neural network weights mostly uses local maths and memorised dataset patterns, not deep reasoning.
ai.summary: Researchers gave an AI the full text of small neural networks' weights and asked it to interpret them without tools or dataset names. It could do simple local calculations and spot some output patterns, but often guessed the wrong dataset or class, suggesting it relied on memorised priors rather than tracing how information flows through the network.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that claims about AI 'reading' brain-like networks should be treated cautiously, since the AI may be pattern-matching rather than truly understanding.
ai.life_skill: Check whether an AI's explanation of a technical system is based on tracing the actual steps or just repeating familiar patterns.
ai.fact: Large language models can perform some local arithmetic on neural network weights but often misidentify the underlying dataset or task.

quiz.question: What did the researchers conclude about the AI's ability to read neural network weights?
quiz.answer: It was better described as local arithmetic plus memorised dataset priors than as tracing weight flows through the network.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, based on exploratory results from mostly single runs.

items.title: DB-ATRG: The Density and BI-RADS-Aware Triage and Automatic Report Generation System for Mammography

ai.headline: An AI tool can prioritise urgent mammograms and draft reports faster than standard queues.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a system called DB-ATRG that uses AI to generate mammography reports and rank cases by urgency. In a simulation of 100 cases, it caught all high-risk cancers within the first fifth of the workload, compared with only 19.2% under a standard first-in, first-out queue.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI might help overstretched radiology services spot serious breast cancer cases sooner.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the results come from a simulated cohort rather than real patients.

items.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex

ai.headline: New open AI models called Drex choose answers from options quickly and consistently without long reasoning chains.
ai.summary: The paper introduces Drex, a family of four open decision models that take a document or image and return a probability distribution over user-supplied options instead of generating long text. Testing shows the largest model is fast, stable when options are reordered, and competitive with other leading decision models on benchmark tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI tools used for everyday choices could become faster and more reliable by avoiding unpredictable long-form reasoning.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI tool gives the same answer when you reorder the options it is choosing between.
ai.fact: Drex Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, much faster than the comparison models GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5.

quiz.question: What does a Drex decision model return instead of a long generated answer?
quiz.answer: It returns a probability distribution over the options supplied by the user.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from benchmarks selected by the authors rather than independent real-world trials.

items.title: Habitat degradation destabilizes complex metacommunities by disrupting dispersal

ai.headline: Habitat loss and fragmentation can push ecosystems from stable to unstable by disrupting how species move between patches.
ai.summary: The study used a mathematical model of connected ecological communities to explore how habitat degradation affects stability after disturbances like drought or fire. It found that dispersal can shift communities from unstable to reactive or stable states, while habitat loss and fragmentation can drive extinctions by pushing communities toward instability.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that breaking up habitats can be as damaging as losing habitat outright, helping us understand how human changes to landscapes affect the survival of species.
ai.life_skill: Notice how connected green spaces are in your area and consider whether wildlife can move between them.
ai.fact: Habitat fragmentation can drive species extinctions even when the total amount of habitat lost is the same.

quiz.question: What does the study say about fragmentation compared with habitat loss?
quiz.answer: Fragmentation can be just as effective as habitat loss at driving species extinctions by shifting communities toward instability.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a mathematical model, not peer-reviewed evidence from real ecosystems.

items.title: Harnessing the personal health data explosion

ai.headline: More people track health with apps and wearables, while social media spreads both useful and inaccurate health claims.
ai.summary: The article describes how smart watches, fitness apps and social media have increased access to personal health data. It notes that health workers face growing challenges as inaccurate health posts spread online, and it reports a debate among doctors about whether to engage with influencers or avoid regulatory risks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why people need to judge online health information carefully and know when to seek professional advice.
ai.life_skill: Check health claims you see online against advice from a qualified health professional before acting on them.
ai.fact: Smart watches, health and fitness apps and social media have increased people’s access to personal health information.

quiz.question: What challenge do health workers face as personal health data and social media use grow?
quiz.answer: They face accumulating challenges from inaccurate health posts online and debate over whether doctors should correct misinformation or engage with influencers.

ai.caveat: This is a feature article and commentary, not a research study with measured results, so it does not prove any effect.

items.title: From rule application to understanding the parties: scenario-based learning and self-reported general empathy among law students

ai.headline: Scenario-based classroom learning is linked to higher self-reported empathy among law students.
ai.summary: Researchers randomly assigned undergraduate law students to either scenario-based learning or a control group. The scenario-based group reported higher general empathy after the course, along with greater cognitive engagement and attention to the situation.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that practising real-life case scenarios can help people shift from simply applying rules to considering other people’s circumstances.
ai.life_skill: Try discussing real-life scenarios with others to notice how different people’s circumstances affect their choices.
ai.fact: The study used the Chinese revised Basic Empathy Scale to measure self-reported general empathy.

quiz.question: What did the scenario-based learning group report compared with the control group?
quiz.answer: They reported higher post-test self-reported general empathy in legal-case contexts.

ai.caveat: Mediators and outcome were measured at the same time after the intervention, so the study cannot prove that scenario-based learning caused the empathy increase or any psychological mechanism.

items.title: COVID-19-related stress linked to faster epigenetic aging in adolescents

ai.headline: COVID-19-related stress is linked to faster epigenetic ageing in adolescents.
ai.summary: Researchers studied adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic and found that pandemic-related stress was linked to faster epigenetic ageing, especially among this age group.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that major social stress can leave measurable biological marks on young people's bodies.
ai.life_skill: Notice when stress is building up and talk to a trusted adult or counsellor about it.
ai.fact: Epigenetic ageing is a biological measure that can be influenced by stress.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about COVID-19-related stress in adolescents?
quiz.answer: It was linked to faster epigenetic ageing.

ai.caveat: This summary is based on a news report, not the full peer-reviewed study, so the methods and strength of the link are unclear.

items.title: Autistic children benefited from online literacy instruction during COVID pandemic

ai.headline: Autistic children made significant literacy progress through online teaching during COVID-19 lockdowns.
ai.summary: A feasibility study looked at autistic children receiving online literacy instruction while at home during COVID-19 restrictions. Despite obstacles, the children showed significant progress in literacy.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that online literacy teaching can work for autistic children even when in-person lessons are not possible.
ai.life_skill: Try practising reading or spelling online using simple, structured lessons if in-person teaching is unavailable.
ai.fact: Autistic children involved in a feasibility study showed significant progress through online literacy instruction during COVID-19 lockdowns.

quiz.question: What did autistic children in the study show through online literacy instruction?
quiz.answer: They showed significant progress despite the obstacles of being at home during COVID-19 lockdowns.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a feasibility study, not peer-reviewed proof that online instruction caused the progress.

items.title: Person-Environment Fit for Persons With Dementia

ai.headline: A telehealth occupational therapy trial for dementia is testing whether it can improve behaviour and daily function.
ai.summary: This is a planned randomised trial involving 38 pairs of people with Alzheimer’s disease or related dementias and their caregivers. One group will receive an 8-week telehealth occupational therapy intervention via Zoom, while the other will have 8 telehealth sessions discussing caregiver education with a research assistant.
ai.why_it_matters: It may show whether remote occupational therapy can help people with dementia manage daily life and behavioural symptoms without medication.

quiz.question: How many pairs of participants are involved in this trial?
quiz.answer: The trial will involve 38 dyads, meaning 38 people with dementia and 38 caregivers.

ai.caveat: This is a feasibility trial with results posted, so it tests whether the approach is practical rather than proving it works.

items.title: Scientists turn viruses into weapons against deadly superbugs

ai.headline: Viruses that kill bacteria may help treat antibiotic-resistant infections, with early guidelines now available.
ai.summary: Researchers are studying phage therapy, which uses viruses to target and kill harmful bacteria. Early results show improvement in 77% of patients and disappearance of targeted bacteria in 61%. International guidelines have been released to help bring this experimental treatment into clinical practice safely.
ai.why_it_matters: This offers a potential new option for infections that do not respond to antibiotics, which could affect everyday health in the future.
ai.life_skill: Try learning how antibiotic resistance happens so you can use antibiotics only when a qualified professional says they are needed.
ai.fact: Phage therapy uses viruses that specifically target and kill harmful bacteria.

quiz.question: What did early findings report about patients receiving phage therapy?
quiz.answer: Early findings reported improvement in 77% of patients and disappearance of targeted bacteria in 61%.

ai.caveat: This is a news report summarising early findings, not peer-reviewed proof that the treatment works.

items.title: [Perspectives] Tobacco exposure: online exhibitions at CSTS

ai.headline: Tobacco remains a preventable global pandemic causing an estimated one billion deaths this century.
ai.summary: The paper notes that although adult smoking has fallen in many high-income countries, tobacco still causes a huge global burden of death. It describes the issue as an entirely preventable pandemic.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that tobacco use is still a major worldwide health problem even where fewer adults smoke.
ai.life_skill: Notice how tobacco use affects people around you and consider reliable sources if you want to understand its risks.
ai.fact: Tobacco-attributed mortality has been estimated at one billion lives for the 21st century.

quiz.question: What does the paper call the global burden of tobacco-attributed mortality?
quiz.answer: An entirely preventable pandemic.

ai.caveat: This is a short perspective piece, not a study with new data or a systematic review.

items.title: Microplastics may be changing the colour of the Pacific Ocean

ai.headline: Satellites suggest microplastics are changing the colour and brightness of the Pacific Ocean.
ai.summary: Researchers used satellite data to observe the ocean around a large gyre of plastic waste in the Pacific. They found that the water in this area is brightening and changing colour, which is most likely caused by suspended microplastics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that plastic pollution is not just a surface issue but is altering the physical properties of the ocean itself.
ai.life_skill: Notice how local plastic waste might affect nearby water bodies or ecosystems.
ai.fact: Microplastics suspended in the water column can change the way light interacts with the ocean.

quiz.question: What is the most likely cause of the colour change in the Pacific gyre?
quiz.answer: The most likely explanation is microplastics suspended in the water column.

ai.caveat: This is a news report describing satellite observations, not a peer-reviewed study, and the link is described as the 'most likely explanation' rather than proven causation.

items.title: Are brain-scanning hard hats a safety dream—or a privacy nightmare?

ai.headline: Some construction and mining firms use brain-scanning hard hats to track worker fatigue, raising privacy concerns.
ai.summary: This news report describes construction and mining firms introducing brain-scanning hard hats to monitor workers’ fatigue. It notes that critics warn the technology could be misused by authorities. No research findings, numbers, or study details are provided.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how new workplace technology can improve safety while also creating privacy risks for workers.
ai.life_skill: Check your workplace’s policy on wearable monitoring and ask what data is collected and who can see it.
ai.fact: Some construction and mining companies are using brain-scanning hard hats to track workers’ fatigue.

quiz.question: What are critics worried about with brain-scanning hard hats?
quiz.answer: Critics say the technology could be misused by authorities.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a research study, so it provides no evidence about how well the devices work or how often misuse occurs.

items.title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention

ai.headline: Expecting a hard search boosts brain signals at the focus of attention without changing its size.
ai.summary: Researchers tested whether expecting sparse or dense visual search displays changes how attention is spread. Behaviour and EEG showed that expecting a difficult, dense search strengthened neural responses at the cued location but did not narrow or widen the focus of attention. This suggests the brain prepares by turning up the volume on the attended spot rather than adjusting the zoom lens.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how the brain uses expectations to sharpen processing in predictable situations, helping explain focused attention in daily tasks.
ai.life_skill: When you expect a task to be difficult, direct your full attention to the one spot that matters most.
ai.fact: Expecting a difficult visual search increases the strength of attention-related brain signals at the expected location without changing the spatial width of attention.

quiz.question: Did expecting dense displays change the width of attention?
quiz.answer: No, expectancy increased response amplitude at the attended location but did not alter tuning width.

ai.caveat: This is a single laboratory study, so the results may not generalise to every real-world setting.

items.title: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

ai.headline: Calcium heart scans led to the same event rates as traditional checks while recommending fewer statins.
ai.summary: Researchers compared heart scans measuring calcium buildup in arteries with traditional risk assessments in nearly 5,800 adults. Both approaches had the same rate of major cardiovascular events, but scans led to statins being recommended for far fewer patients. People advised to take statins based on their scan were nearly three times more likely to keep taking them.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a scan-based approach could reduce statin prescriptions without worsening outcomes and may improve medication adherence.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified health professional about how your heart disease risk is assessed.
ai.fact: Heart scans can measure calcium buildup in the arteries.

ai.summary: Scientists studied damage to blueberry bushes in North Carolina and found a species of beetle larvae responsible. The larvae can grow up to five inches long and destroy plant roots. Farmers had reported damage for over a decade before the culprit was identified.
ai.why_it_matters: This discovery matters because it can help farmers take action to protect their blueberry crops from destruction.

items.title: Efficacy and Neural Mechanisms of Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) for Depression: A Systematic Review and Qualitative Synthesis.

ai.headline: EMDR may help reduce depressive symptoms, but more high-quality research is needed to confirm it.
ai.summary: A review of 27 studies examined EMDR, a talking therapy originally developed for PTSD, as a treatment for depression. It found EMDR may reduce depressive symptoms across different groups, including people with trauma or other conditions. Early brain research suggests it may involve prefrontal-limbic circuits, but this evidence is preliminary.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a therapy originally made for trauma could broaden treatment options for people living with depression.
ai.life_skill: Notice if low mood or loss of interest persists for weeks and consider speaking with a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: EMDR is a psychotherapy originally developed for post-traumatic stress disorder that is being studied as a treatment for depression.

quiz.question: What did a review of 27 studies find about EMDR and depression?
quiz.answer: It found EMDR may alleviate depressive symptoms, but more large-scale, high-quality studies are needed to confirm this.

ai.caveat: The review included non-randomised studies and the authors call for larger, higher-quality trials to confirm the results and clarify how EMDR works in the brain.

items.title: Human interaction with artificial intelligence as a factor in professional loneliness

ai.headline: AI-mediated work interactions are linked to professional loneliness through lost co-participation, not just fewer contacts.
ai.summary: A systematic review of peer-reviewed studies from 2019 to 2026 examined how AI-mediated interaction at work relates to professional loneliness. It identified four forms: relational energy drain, false connection effect, moral disengagement and responsibility diffusion, and emotional synchrony breakdown. The review concludes it represents a loss of genuine co-participation in professional interaction and authorship of one's own activity.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how AI changes workplace relationships can help people protect their sense of connection and ownership at work.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether using AI at work makes you feel less genuinely involved in your tasks and relationships.
ai.fact: Professional loneliness can reflect a loss of genuine co-participation at work rather than simply having fewer contacts.

quiz.question: What did the review say professional loneliness under AI mediation mainly represents?
quiz.answer: It represents a loss of genuine co-participation in professional interaction and authorship of one's own activity, not just a lack of contacts.

ai.caveat: The review synthesises existing studies and identifies themes, so it does not prove that AI causes loneliness or measure how common it is.

items.title: Systematic review of digital governance and economic transformation in Morocco from 2000 to 2025

ai.headline: Morocco's digital governance has grown unevenly, helping cities more than rural areas.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 51 studies examined digital technology in Morocco's government and economy from 2000 to 2025. It found that digital public services expanded and GDP rose, but cities and the north benefited more than southern and eastern regions.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how technology can improve public services, but also how its benefits can spread unevenly across a country.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether online public services work as well in your area as they do in big cities.
ai.fact: Digital technology in Morocco's public services is concentrated in big cities and northern provinces, with less reach in southern and eastern areas.

quiz.question: Which parts of Morocco received less digital technology according to the review?
quiz.answer: Southern and eastern areas were neglected compared with big cities and northern provinces.

ai.caveat: The review drew on only 51 selected documents and links digital governance to GDP growth without proving it caused the increase.

items.title: Artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and prognosis of leprosy, leishmaniasis, and schistosomiasis: A systematic review

ai.headline: AI tools for three tropical diseases show promise but lack proper testing and transparency.
ai.summary: A review of 69 studies examined AI for diagnosing and predicting leprosy, leishmaniasis, and schistosomiasis. Most models had a high risk of bias because they were not tested on new patients and their code was not shared. The field is growing quickly but is not yet reliable enough for routine healthcare.
ai.why_it_matters: It reminds us that new AI health tools need independent testing and open code before they can be trusted in real clinics.
ai.fact: Most AI models for these three diseases have not been externally validated or made publicly reproducible.

quiz.question: What proportion of the AI models reviewed had a high risk of bias?
quiz.answer: 89.9% of the models were judged to have a high risk of bias.

ai.caveat: The review summarises primary studies that mostly lacked external validation and transparent reporting, so it describes an immature evidence base rather than proven tools.

items.title: A Cluster Randomised Controlled Trial of a Transdiagnostic Preventative Mental Health Intervention for Adolescents: Building Resilience through Socioemotional Training (ReSET)

ai.headline: A school-based mental health programme showed no immediate benefit but reduced symptoms after a year.
ai.summary: Researchers tested an 8-session group programme called ReSET against usual care in 560 at-risk adolescents aged 12–14. There was no improvement immediately after the programme, but at 12-month follow-up the ReSET group reported lower overall psychopathology and benefits for anxiety, depression and internalising symptoms, with no effect on externalising symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that teaching socioemotional skills in schools may help some teenagers’ mental health over time, even when changes are not immediate.
ai.life_skill: Practise noticing and naming your emotions, and share them with someone you trust.
ai.fact: A cluster randomised trial found that a school-based socioemotional programme reduced self-reported psychopathology symptoms in at-risk adolescents 12 months after it ended.

quiz.question: Did the ReSET programme improve mental health immediately after it finished?
quiz.answer: No, there was no evidence of improvement immediately post-intervention, though benefits emerged at 12-month follow-up.

ai.caveat: This is a single preprint that has not yet been peer-reviewed, so the results need replication before being treated as established.

items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI

ai.headline: Giving AI assistants permissioned access to app settings could turn chat into a workspace control panel.
ai.summary: The paper studies 'meta access,' which means giving LLM chat assistants a structured, permissioned view of the software around them, such as settings, messages, and summaries. It proposes this could turn chat into a single control panel for finding, navigating, organizing, and operating a whole workspace, while noting risks to privacy, trust, and accuracy.
ai.why_it_matters: As AI assistants are built into more apps, letting them safely see and change settings could make software easier to control but also creates new privacy and safety issues.
ai.life_skill: Check what permissions an AI assistant has before letting it change settings in your apps.
ai.fact: The paper proposes 'meta access' as a way for AI assistants to view and operate app settings and state with user permission.

quiz.question: What does 'meta access' allow an AI assistant to see?
quiz.answer: It allows the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the software interface around the chat, such as settings and messages.

items.title: A Reproducible Decomposed Large Language Model Pipeline for Structured Abstraction of Multimodal Neuroimaging Reports: Development and Independent Validation in 1,669 Emergency Department Encounters for Dizziness and Vertigo

ai.headline: AI tools can accurately extract specific medical details from complex brain scan reports.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a system that uses AI to pull 22 specific pieces of information from free-text brain scan reports for 1,669 patients with dizziness. The AI’s results were highly consistent and matched the accuracy of human doctors reviewing the same reports.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows how AI can help organise messy medical data, potentially making it easier for researchers to find patterns in large groups of patients.
ai.fact: AI models can extract structured data from medical reports with accuracy comparable to human reviewers.

quiz.question: How did the AI's accuracy compare to human reviewers?
quiz.answer: The AI's accuracy was comparable to the agreement between two human reviewers.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not final.

items.title: Serial dependence carries the action that produced the previous report

ai.headline: Your brain links past actions to current judgments, not just past information.
ai.summary: This preprint tested whether our tendency to be influenced by recent past judgments comes from the information itself or the action used to report it. By having participants use the same physical action (holding a key) to report different types of information, researchers found that the previous action carried over and biased the next judgment, even across different tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that the physical way we interact with the world shapes how we perceive and judge new information, revealing a hidden layer of cognitive bias.
ai.life_skill: Notice if your physical habits or recent actions are subtly influencing how you judge new, unrelated situations.
ai.fact: Serial dependence can carry the trace of the specific action used to express a previous judgment.

quiz.question: Did the study find that the previous stimulus or the previous action caused the bias?
quiz.answer: The study found that the previous action (response) predicted the bias, even when controlling for the previous stimulus.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed by the scientific community.

items.title: Using graphic pathographies as moral dilemma scenarios in medical humanities education: effects on moral distress, need for cognition, and medical mistrust

ai.headline: Using graphic patient stories in medical ethics classes was linked to changes in students' moral distress and thinking habits.
ai.summary: This quasi-experimental study compared medical students who used graphic pathographies (detailed patient stories) as moral dilemma scenarios against a control group using non-graphic scenarios. The researchers found statistically significant differences between the groups in measures of moral distress, need for cognition, and medical mistrust.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that engaging with vivid, real-world narratives can shape how professionals develop their ethical reasoning and critical thinking skills.
ai.life_skill: Notice how reading detailed personal stories about difficult situations can sharpen your ability to think critically about complex problems.
ai.fact: Graphic pathographies are detailed written accounts of a patient's illness and death used to explore ethical issues in medicine.

quiz.question: What type of study design was used to compare the two groups of medical students?
quiz.answer: The research employed a two-group, pre-posttest quasi-experimental study.

ai.caveat: The study was quasi-experimental rather than a randomised trial, so it cannot prove that the graphic pathographies caused the differences, only that they were associated with them.

ai.summary: Researchers studied male Drosophila fruit flies that live on a particular fruit. They found that the smell of that food acts on specific mating circuits in the brain and is needed to begin courtship.

items.title: A systematic review of DoS and DDoS attack detection in cloud environments: evolutionary trends and the emerging role of meta-learning for cross-domain adaptability.

ai.headline: Researchers reviewed 120 papers on detecting DoS and DDoS attacks in cloud systems and found meta-learning may help attacks be spotted across new environments with few examples.
ai.summary: The review traced how detection methods have evolved from early statistical and anomaly-based approaches to machine learning, deep learning and domain-specific systems. Deep learning achieved near-perfect results in experiments, but struggles with generalisation, privacy, efficiency and explainability in real-world cloud settings. Only seven of the 120 studies used meta-learning, transfer learning or few-shot approaches, suggesting these could help detect new attacks across different domains with limited labelled data.
ai.why_it_matters: Cloud outages from attacks can disrupt everyday services people rely on, so better detection methods matter for keeping online systems available and reliable.
ai.life_skill: Notice when online services you use become slow or unreachable, and report it to the provider rather than assuming it is your own connection.
ai.fact: DoS and DDoS attacks aim to disrupt the availability of network services rather than steal data directly.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the use of meta-learning in the 120 studies examined?
quiz.answer: Only seven studies used meta-learning, transfer learning or few-shot approaches explicitly.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on a review of existing studies rather than new experiments, and the authors propose meta-learning as promising rather than proving it works in real-world deployment.

items.title: Personality determinants of the experience of loneliness in adolescents in the digital world

ai.headline: Personality traits shape how digital environments affect loneliness in teenagers.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined international research on personality-based predictors of adolescent loneliness in digital environments. It found that personality traits mediate the relationship between digital behaviour and feelings of loneliness, with the digital environment having both positive and negative effects.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that loneliness online is not just about how much time is spent online, but about individual personality characteristics.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your personality traits, such as self-esteem or social confidence, affect how you feel after using digital platforms.
ai.fact: Personality traits act as a mediator between digital behaviours and feelings of loneliness in adolescents.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the relationship between digital behaviour and loneliness?
quiz.answer: Personality traits mediate the relationship between digital behaviours and feelings of loneliness.

ai.caveat: The review synthesises existing studies rather than providing new experimental proof, and the findings are correlational rather than causal.

items.title: Interconnected Mental Health Stressors and Risks in Returnee Nepalese Migrant Workers: A Focus Group Study

ai.headline: Returnee Nepalese migrant workers face linked stressors including exploitation, poor work conditions, family strain and suicide risk.
ai.summary: This qualitative study held seven focus groups with returnee Nepalese migrant workers who had worked in GCC countries and Malaysia. It found six interconnected themes affecting mental health: accommodation and communication, occupational health, exploitation at work, family at home, leisure and coping, and suicide narratives and support.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how work, family and social conditions combine to affect the mental wellbeing of people who migrate for work.
ai.life_skill: Notice how work conditions, family contact and coping habits are connected to your own stress levels.
ai.fact: The study identified six interconnected themes linked to social determinants of mental health among returnee Nepalese migrant workers.

quiz.question: What did the study find about the sources of stress for returnee Nepalese migrant workers?
quiz.answer: Six interconnected themes—accommodation and communication, occupational health, exploitation at work, family at home, leisure coping and risk behaviours, and suicide narratives and support—were linked to their mental health.

ai.caveat: It is a small qualitative focus-group study of returnees only, so current workers abroad may have different experiences and the findings cannot prove cause and effect.

items.title: AVISNet: An edge-computing model for acoustic identification of species from the Doñana bird community

ai.headline: A lightweight AI model identifies bird species from sound on small, low-power devices without needing the cloud.
ai.summary: Researchers built AVISNet, an edge-computing model that runs automated acoustic bird identification directly on embedded devices. Tested on birds from Doñana National Park, Spain, it reached up to 0.70 F1-score on focal recordings and 0.56–0.72 at soundscape dataset level, while being 2.2–4.7 times faster and using 41–71% less energy than BirdNET.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how wildlife monitoring can become cheaper, faster and more independent of internet connections, helping track biodiversity in remote areas.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing bird sounds around you and consider how technology could help identify local species without disturbing them.
ai.fact: Birds are sensitive ecological indicators whose vocal activity makes them well suited for passive acoustic monitoring.

quiz.question: What did AVISNet achieve on focal recordings for bird species identification?
quiz.answer: The models achieved up to 0.70 F1-score in species identification on focal recordings.

ai.caveat: This is a single modelling study applied to one bird community, so results may not generalise to other species or habitats.

items.title: Ocular Phototherapy and Mental Health: What Vision Scientists and Clinicians Need to Know

ai.headline: Bright light therapy can help depression, but the right dose depends on your eyes, age and the light’s colour.
ai.summary: The paper reviews research on how light entering the eye affects mood through special retinal cells. It finds that blue-appearing light works better than dim red light for seasonal affective disorder, but not clearly better than white light, and that older eyes receive roughly half the light dose by age 75.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that light therapy is a real, low-cost option for some depression, but its effects depend on physical factors like age and light spectrum rather than being one-size-fits-all.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether the light you use for mood is bright white and positioned to reach your eyes, rather than dim or strongly coloured.
ai.fact: Melatonin suppression by light peaks at around 446–477 nanometres.

quiz.question: Does blue-appearing light clearly outperform broadband white light for seasonal affective disorder?
quiz.answer: No, it has not outperformed broadband white light.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review and preprint, not peer-reviewed, so it summarises existing research rather than proving new effects.

items.title: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer

ai.headline: A brain-like system using repeating memory cycles can solve new, much longer problems after short training.
ai.summary: The paper studies how learners handle inputs longer than anything they have seen before. It finds that systems reading only whether things match, rather than counting positions, can keep the same rule at any size; a cycle-based model trained on strings up to 40 symbols was at least 99% accurate on average across lengths 41 to 500 for nine of fifteen tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a way of thinking—spotting sameness instead of tracking position—that may help people tackle unfamiliar, larger versions of problems they already know.
ai.life_skill: When facing a bigger version of a task, check what stays the same rather than counting where you are.
ai.fact: A cycle-based memory model trained on strings up to 40 symbols solved strings up to 500 symbols with at least 99% average accuracy on nine of fifteen tasks.

quiz.question: What does a learner that reads only coincidences find in a long input that short inputs lacked?
quiz.answer: It finds nothing that short inputs lacked, so short experience fixes its rule for every size.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is based on theory and simulations rather than human trials.

items.title: Automated Segmentation of Intracranial Arteries on 4D Flow MRI for Hemodynamic Quantification

ai.headline: An AI method for mapping brain arteries on high-resolution MRI scans matched manual results better than two other automated methods.
ai.summary: Researchers compared three computer models for outlining brain arteries on 7T 4D Flow MRI scans. A transfer-learning nnU-Net trained on 11 scans performed best, agreeing closely with manual outlines for vessel area, blood flow and wall shear stress, while the other two models under- or over-estimated some measures.
ai.why_it_matters: Better automated brain-vessel mapping could make advanced MRI studies faster and less dependent on individual operators, supporting future research into brain blood flow and health.

quiz.question: Which automated segmentation model agreed most closely with the manual reference for blood flow and wall shear stress?
quiz.answer: The transfer learning-based nnU-Net model showed the closest agreement with the manual reference.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed and was based on a small set of 11 scans, so the findings are preliminary.

items.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI

ai.headline: A new method helps AI robots keep old skills while learning new ones without forgetting.
ai.summary: The paper studies continual learning for physical AI robots, where small mistakes can build up and cause task failure. It introduces DRAP, which protects important model parts linked to risky moments, and shows it retains old behaviours better than standard fine-tuning and EWC while still learning new tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI systems might learn new tasks without losing previously useful abilities, relevant to understanding adaptive technology.
ai.life_skill: Notice when small mistakes in a repeated task can build up into bigger problems.
ai.fact: Small per-step errors in physical AI can accumulate over a trajectory and lead to closed-loop task failure.

quiz.question: What problem does DRAP aim to reduce in physical AI continual learning?
quiz.answer: It aims to reduce forgetting of previously learned behaviours while learning new tasks.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and based on simulations rather than real-world trials.

items.title: Effects of Social Prescribing for Older Adults: An Evidence and Gap Map

ai.headline: A large evidence map finds social prescribing research for older adults is mostly low quality and concentrated in wealthy countries.

items.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure

ai.headline: AI exposure is linked to less dull, dirty, and dangerous work, but the link weakens after accounting for job traits.
ai.summary: The study looked at 754 US occupations and 21 work-condition items to see how AI exposure relates to dull, dirty, and dangerous jobs. Higher AI exposure was associated with lower scores on these conditions, but adjusting for physical demands, education, training, experience, and wages reduced the association, with some results no longer clearly different from zero.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that claims about AI freeing people from unpleasant work depend on how job conditions are measured and what other job features are considered.
ai.life_skill: Check how a job is described before assuming automation will remove its dull, dirty, or dangerous parts.
ai.fact: AI exposure estimates can change depending on which work-condition items are grouped together and which occupational traits are adjusted for.

quiz.question: What happened to the link between AI exposure and dull, dirty, and dangerous conditions after adjusting for job traits?
quiz.answer: The association was reduced, and for the LLM measure the adjusted confidence intervals included zero.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and the findings are associations from one US dataset rather than proof that AI causes relief from unpleasant work.

items.title: Maternal ADHD and exclusive breastfeeding: A prospective community-based cohort study

ai.headline: Mothers with ADHD are less likely to breastfeed exclusively for six months despite intending to do so.
ai.summary: This Canadian study followed over 3,000 mother-father pairs from shortly after birth. Among mothers who screened positive for ADHD, only 28% breastfed exclusively for six months, compared with a higher rate among mothers without ADHD.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that good intentions may not be enough and that parents with ADHD may need extra, tailored support to keep breastfeeding.
ai.life_skill: If you are a new parent with ADHD, ask a midwife, health visitor or lactation consultant for practical breastfeeding support early on.
ai.fact: Maternal ADHD is an established risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes.

quiz.question: What percentage of mothers with ADHD breastfed exclusively for six months in this study?
quiz.answer: Only 28% of mothers with ADHD breastfed exclusively for six months.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it is an observational study, so it cannot prove that ADHD caused the shorter breastfeeding duration.

items.title: RECOVER-ENERGIZE Platform Protocol

ai.headline: A trial is testing treatments to improve exercise tolerance and quality of life in people with Long COVID.
ai.summary: The RECOVER-ENERGIZE platform trial is a randomized, controlled study evaluating different interventions for exercise intolerance and post-exertional malaise in patients with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection. It aims to see whether these interventions can improve exercise capacity, tolerance of daily activities, and quality of life.
ai.why_it_matters: It may help identify safe, effective ways for people recovering from Long COVID to manage physical activity and daily life.
ai.life_skill: If you have ongoing fatigue or breathlessness after COVID, discuss activity management with a qualified healthcare professional.
ai.fact: Post-exertional malaise is a symptom being studied in people with Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection.

quiz.question: What is the RECOVER-ENERGIZE trial testing?
quiz.answer: It is testing interventions to improve exercise capacity, daily activities tolerance, and quality of life in people with Long COVID.

ai.caveat: This is a protocol describing a planned trial, so results are not yet available.

items.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?

ai.headline: Multi-turn AI agent training helps mainly when agents have enough turns to recover from mistakes.
ai.summary: The study looked at how training AI agents with multi-turn reinforcement learning affects their performance on long tasks. It found that improvements depend heavily on having enough interaction turns, and that the main benefits are in recovering from errors and handling long tasks rather than improving every single decision.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that AI assistants may work well only when given enough time and steps to fix mistakes, which matters for how we use them in daily life.
ai.life_skill: When using an AI agent for a complex task, give it enough turns or steps to correct its own mistakes rather than expecting perfection on the first try.
ai.fact: Multi-turn reinforcement learning advantages for AI agents concentrate in error recovery and long-horizon resilience rather than uniformly improving single-step decisions.

quiz.question: Where does multi-turn reinforcement learning mainly help AI agents, according to the study?
quiz.answer: Its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience rather than uniformly improving single-step decision quality.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are preliminary and not yet confirmed.

items.title: We need to build risk management into training curriculums

ai.headline: GP training curriculums should teach risk management more explicitly across all areas of practice.
ai.summary: The article argues that holding risk is fundamental to general practice because GPs make many daily decisions, yet current training curriculums include only one learning outcome about risk. It suggests risk management should be built into more curriculum domains, including documentation and supervision, not just patient management.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how professionals learn to handle uncertainty and make safer everyday decisions in high-stakes work.
ai.life_skill: Notice where you are making decisions with incomplete information and pause to consider the risks before acting.
ai.fact: General practitioners make a high volume of daily decisions that involve managing risk and uncertainty.

quiz.question: How many learning outcomes about risk does the GP registrar curriculum currently include, according to the article?
quiz.answer: It includes only one learning outcome that discusses risk.

ai.caveat: This is an opinion piece from a journal, not a research study with data or tested results.

items.title: Trust in influencers grows more important in predicting buying intentions over time, analysis finds

ai.headline: Trust in influencers becomes more important for predicting buying intentions over time, a meta-analysis finds.
ai.summary: A meta-analysis of empirical studies with over 31,000 participants examined factors affecting social media influencers' impact. Credibility, expertise, attractiveness and perceived similarity were positively linked to consumers' attitudes toward promoted brands and, in turn, their purchasing intentions.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how social media personalities can shape what young people want to buy, helping them recognise why they feel drawn to certain products.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you trust an influencer because they seem credible, expert, attractive or similar to you before you decide to buy something they promote.
ai.fact: Credibility, expertise, attractiveness and perceived similarity are positively associated with consumer attitudes toward brands promoted by influencers and with purchasing intentions.

quiz.question: What did the meta-analysis find about factors like credibility and expertise in relation to buying intentions?
quiz.answer: They are positively associated with consumers' attitudes toward brands promoted by influencers and, in turn, with their purchasing intentions.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on a meta-analysis of existing empirical studies, so they show associations rather than proving that influencer trust causes buying decisions.

items.title: Polycomb Marked Promoter Methylation Gains in Aging and Cancer are Independent of Replication

ai.headline: Cancer-linked DNA changes may come from ageing rather than the cancer gene itself.
ai.summary: Researchers tracked DNA methylation in mouse colon stem-cell clones with and without a cancer-linked BRAF gene switch. Both groups developed similar methylation gains at Polycomb-marked promoters over time, independent of cell division, while the cancer gene mainly selected and expanded existing clones.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests some early cancer biomarkers may reflect biological ageing rather than being directly caused by cancer signals.
ai.fact: Polycomb-marked promoter methylation gains can occur with biological ageing independently of cell replication.

quiz.question: Did BRAFV600E induction actively create Polycomb-marked promoter methylation gains?
quiz.answer: No, these gains tracked with biological ageing independent of replication and were not induced or accelerated by BRAFV600E.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and was done in mouse colon organoids, so findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise

ai.headline: Viruses and bacteria work together to kill algae faster, speeding up the collapse of ocean algal blooms.
ai.summary: The study looked at how viruses and bacteria interact during algal blooms in the ocean. It found that bacteria called Alteromonas are attracted to infected algae and help viruses kill them more quickly, causing blooms to collapse faster.
ai.why_it_matters: This helps scientists understand how carbon moves through the ocean and how marine ecosystems change.
ai.fact: Viral–bacterial synergy can accelerate algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality.

quiz.question: What effect does the synergy between viruses and bacteria have on algal blooms?
quiz.answer: It accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a single study and may not apply to all ocean environments.

items.title: Generative AI fills gaps in brain wiring maps where MRI scans lose signal

ai.headline: AI fills gaps in brain wiring maps
ai.summary: Researchers developed an AI model to improve brain wiring maps made with diffusion MRI scans. This model helps fill gaps in these maps where MRI scans lose signal. The goal is to study changes in brain connections with aging and disease.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because understanding brain connections can help researchers study aging and disease
ai.fact: Diffusion MRI scans can lose signal and miss details in brain wiring maps

quiz.question: What type of scan can lose signal and miss details in brain wiring maps?
quiz.answer: Diffusion MRI scans

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a development, not a peer-reviewed study, so the findings have not been fully vetted by the scientific community

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage

ai.headline: AI helped scientists find a natural molecule that reduced appetite and fat loss in animals without common side effects.
ai.summary: Stanford researchers used AI to identify a natural molecule called BRP. In animal studies, BRP cut food intake by up to 50% and promoted fat loss without the usual digestive side effects or significant muscle loss linked to Ozempic-like drugs.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI can speed up the search for new treatments that might one day help people manage weight more precisely.
ai.fact: BRP targets a different brain pathway than current Ozempic-like weight-loss drugs.

quiz.question: What did BRP do in animal studies?
quiz.answer: It reduced food intake by up to 50% and promoted fat loss without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss.

ai.caveat: The findings are from animals only, so they may not apply to humans until clinical trials are completed.

items.title: Global temperature-related mortality associated with El-Nino Southern Oscillation

ai.headline: El Niño linked to heat deaths
ai.summary: Researchers studied global temperature-related mortality and its association with the El-Nino Southern Oscillation. They found that heat-related mortality increased during very strong El Niño years. The greatest burdens occurred in low- and medium- Human Development Index regions.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it helps us understand how climate patterns affect human health and mortality rates worldwide
ai.life_skill: Check weather forecasts to prepare for extreme heat
ai.fact: El Niño is linked to increased global heat-related mortality

quiz.question: What happens to global heat-related mortality during very strong El Niño years?
quiz.answer: It increases by 29%

ai.caveat: This study is an observational estimate and does not prove a direct causal link between El Niño and heat-related mortality

items.title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation

ai.headline: Bacteria sporulate via peptidoglycan degradation
ai.summary: Researchers studied bacterial sporulation in Myxococcus xanthus, finding it occurs through peptidoglycan degradation by two lytic transglycosylases. This process is regulated by the interaction between the two enzymes and peptidoglycan synthesis. The findings reveal a novel mechanism for bacterial sporulation.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding bacterial sporulation can help develop new strategies to combat bacterial infections and improve our knowledge of microbial biology.
ai.fact: Bacteria can form spores to endure unfavorable conditions through a process called sporulation.

quiz.question: What triggers sporulation in Myxococcus xanthus?
quiz.answer: Sporulation in Myxococcus xanthus is triggered by chemical induction or starvation.

ai.caveat: This study was conducted in a specific bacterium and may not be generalizable to all bacteria.

items.title: Risk and Return in Government Bonds -- by Matteo Leombroni, Carolin Pflueger, Adi Sunderam

ai.headline: The extra return investors demand for government bonds moves closely with how risky those bonds are.
ai.summary: Researchers studied U.S. government bonds from 1988 to 2024 and found that expected excess returns are tightly linked to bond–stock betas, a standard measure of risk. The relationship holds across developed countries, and changing bond risk explains more than half of the fall in long-term U.S. bond yields since the mid-1980s and their rise since 2020.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how perceptions of risk shape the interest rates governments pay, which affects borrowing costs for everyone.
ai.life_skill: Notice that bond prices and yields move with market risk, not just with central bank decisions.
ai.fact: Expected excess returns on government bonds are tightly linked to their betas with the stock market.

quiz.question: What measure of risk did the researchers link to expected excess returns on government bonds?
quiz.answer: Bonds’ betas with respect to the stock market.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings show a link rather than proof that risk causes the return.

items.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to autism's origins hidden in the placenta

ai.headline: Pregnancy inflammation and placental damage are linked to autism-like traits in male mice, not females.
ai.summary: Researchers studied mice exposed to inflammation during pregnancy and found placental damage and autism-like traits in males, while females appeared protected. The findings may help explain why autism is diagnosed more often in boys.
ai.why_it_matters: It points to a possible early biological clue for autism and highlights sex differences in brain development.
ai.fact: In male mice, inflammation during pregnancy was linked to placental damage and autism-like traits, while female mice appeared protected.

quiz.question: Which mice showed autism-like traits after pregnancy inflammation?
quiz.answer: Male mice showed autism-like traits, while females appeared protected.

ai.caveat: The study was in mice, so the results may not apply to humans.

items.title: Hunt for natural hydrogen, an elusive clean fuel, hits roadblocks

ai.headline: Searching for natural hydrogen as a clean fuel faces challenges, but a French borehole shows promise.
ai.summary: Prospectors looking for natural hydrogen are encountering difficulties. A new borehole in France suggests that extracting hydrogen gas from groundwater may be possible.

ai.fact: Natural hydrogen is being explored as a potential clean fuel.

items.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Scribe for Clinical Notes

ai.summary: The paper describes the use of an artificial intelligence scribe for generating clinical notes. It reports on how this tool was applied in practice to support documentation.

quiz.question: What was the AI scribe used for?

items.title: Stunning collection of prehistoric engravings found in Spanish cave

ai.summary: Researchers examined a frequently visited cave wall in Spain and discovered a striking collection of rock art engravings. The engravings are thought to be at least 19,000 years old.

ai.fact: Rock art engravings in a Spanish cave are thought to be at least 19,000 years old.

quiz.answer: They are thought to be at least 19,000 years old.

ai.headline: MIT’s annual energy conference covered nuclear power, quantum computing and future energy technologies.
ai.summary: The MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference brought together discussion of today’s energy technologies, including a nuclear revival, and early-stage research such as qubits for tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

ai.fact: MIT’s Energy Initiative holds an annual research conference on current and future energy technologies.

quiz.answer: Today’s energy technologies, including nuclear power, and future research such as qubits.
