items.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'

ai.headline: Typhoons in East Asia have been unusually severe recently, linked to El Niño warming the Pacific.
ai.summary: The report describes unusually wild weather and typhoons affecting East Asian countries where typhoons are common. It connects this activity to El Niño, a climate pattern that warms the Pacific Ocean.

ai.fact: El Niño is a climate pattern associated with warmer-than-usual Pacific Ocean temperatures.

items.title: School-Based Educational Interventions for Improving Knowledge of Back Health, Ergonomics and Postural Behaviour of School Children Aged 4-18 Years: A Best Evidence Systematic Review

ai.headline: School lessons on back health and posture may improve children’s knowledge and behaviour.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined high-quality trials of school-based education programmes teaching back health, ergonomics and posture to children aged 4–18. The included studies compared these programmes with usual teaching or a wait-list and looked at knowledge and postural behaviour.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows whether classroom teaching can help young people understand how to sit, stand and move in ways that may protect their backs.
ai.life_skill: Notice how you sit at your desk and adjust your chair and screen so your back feels supported.
ai.fact: Musculoskeletal and back problems are increasingly reported in children and young people, not only adults.

quiz.question: What did the school programmes in this review aim to improve?
quiz.answer: They aimed to improve knowledge of back health, ergonomics and postural behaviour in school children aged 4–18.

items.title: Free/low-cost physical activity opportunities for children and adolescents: Parental perspectives on participation, access and provision

ai.headline: Most parents use free or low-cost activity for their children, but say local options are not enough.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 855 parents and interviewed 29 parents in Northern Ireland about free or low-cost physical activity for children aged 4–16. Nearly all children took part weekly, usually through walking and outdoor play, yet 76% of parents felt local opportunities were insufficient and only 10% thought provision was adequate.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that making activities free does not by itself guarantee easy access for every family.
ai.life_skill: Check what free or low-cost activities are available near you and try walking or outdoor play as a regular option.
ai.fact: Almost all parents in the study reported weekly participation in at least one free or low-cost physical activity opportunity for their child.

quiz.question: What did most parents say about local free or low-cost activity opportunities?
quiz.answer: Most parents felt there were not enough local opportunities, with only 10% considering provision adequate.

ai.caveat: This is a cross-sectional questionnaire and interview study from one region, so it shows links and experiences rather than proving cause and effect.

items.title: Competition pressure and psychological resilience among university teachers: a mixed-methods study of teaching competitions in Chinese higher education

ai.headline: Teaching competition stress peaks mid-event and resilience support needs to match timing and individual teachers.
ai.summary: Researchers studied university teachers taking part in teaching competitions using interviews and questionnaires. They found competition pressure followed an inverted U-shape, peaking at the provincial selection stage, and that psychological resilience worked differently depending on the situation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that pressure during high-stakes events changes over time and that support should be tailored to when people need it most.
ai.life_skill: Notice when your stress rises during a big challenge and plan extra support around that peak moment.
ai.fact: Competition pressure among university teachers peaked at the provincial competition selection stage, averaging 8.2 points.

quiz.question: When did competition pressure peak for the university teachers in the study?
quiz.answer: Pressure peaked at the provincial competition selection stage.

ai.caveat: This is a single mixed-methods study with interviews and questionnaires from one context, so it cannot prove that competition pressure causes changes in resilience.

items.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial

ai.headline: Cryotherapy worked as well as anesthetic sprays or gels for children’s dental pain and anxiety, with better treatment compliance.
ai.summary: A randomised trial of 100 children aged 7–10 compared cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, anesthetic gel, and cooled anesthetic spray before dental treatment. No significant differences were found between groups for anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability, but cryotherapy with distilled water had higher treatment compliance scores than gel or cooled spray.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a simple, non-drug option may help children cope with dental treatment, though more confirmation is needed.
ai.life_skill: Ask a qualified dental professional whether non-drug options such as cooling might suit a child’s dental care.
ai.fact: Cryotherapy-distilled water produced significantly higher treatment compliance scores than benzocaine gel or cooled lidocaine spray (p = 0.001).

quiz.question: Did cryotherapy differ significantly from anesthetic agents for pain and anxiety?
quiz.answer: No, pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents.

ai.caveat: The compliance finding was described as exploratory and needs confirmation in non-inferiority trials.

items.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution

ai.headline: A new AI method helps software agents learn from their own past experiences more efficiently.
ai.summary: The study tested MDSKILL, a method that organises an AI agent’s skill memories into three views—state grounding, action planning, and execution control—to improve how it learns from its own experiences. On three agent benchmarks, it improved performance by up to 7.1% on ALFWorld and 8.1% on WebShop without extra computing cost.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI systems can get better at independent tasks by learning from their own history, which matters as such agents are used more in everyday digital tools.
ai.life_skill: Try reviewing your own past attempts at a digital task to spot what worked and what did not before trying again.
ai.fact: Organising skill memories into state grounding, action planning, and execution control views can improve AI agent learning.

quiz.question: What did MDSKILL do with skill memories to help AI agents learn better?
quiz.answer: It organised them into three complementary views—state grounding, action planning, and execution control—and distilled knowledge across them into a shared policy.

ai.caveat: This is a computer-science modelling study with benchmark results, not evidence about human learning or behaviour.

items.title: Motivational Incongruence Predicts Subsequent Psychological Distress in Psychotherapy: Within-Person Evidence From Three Samples

ai.headline: Reductions in motivational incongruence during therapy were linked to later reductions in psychological distress.
ai.summary: The study looked at three psychotherapy samples with 1,656 patients, measuring motivational incongruence and distress several times during treatment. It found that when a person’s motivational incongruence went down, their general psychological distress tended to go down afterwards. Distress also predicted later incongruence in two of the three samples.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that helping people align their motives with their environment could be a useful focus in therapy for reducing distress.
ai.life_skill: Notice when your goals and daily life feel mismatched, and consider discussing this mismatch with a qualified therapist or counsellor.
ai.fact: Motivational incongruence means a person’s motives are not sufficiently satisfied through their interactions with their environment.

quiz.question: What did the study find about motivational incongruence and distress?
quiz.answer: Within-person reductions in motivational incongruence preceded reductions in general psychological distress across the samples.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the findings come from observational models rather than proof that changing incongruence causes distress to fall.

items.title: Factors Associated with Meaning in Life Among Hispanic Adults in the Post-Pandemic Period: A Cross-Sectional Study Across 16 Countries

ai.headline: About half of Hispanic adults across 16 countries reported low meaning in life after the pandemic.
ai.summary: A cross-sectional study of 10,142 Hispanic adults aged 18 to 78 across 16 countries examined meaning in life after the pandemic. About half reported low meaning in life, which was linked to better mental health, occupational purpose, gratitude, friendships, and meaningful activities, while low workplace success, no gratitude, and heavy social media use were linked to lower meaning.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling life is meaningful may depend more on relationships and daily habits than on income or education.
ai.life_skill: Notice which activities and friendships make your days feel meaningful and make time for them.
ai.fact: In this study, income, education, and gender were not significantly linked to meaning in life.

quiz.question: What percentage of participants reported low levels of meaning in life?
quiz.answer: 50.2% of participants experienced low levels of meaning in life.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and a single cross-sectional study cannot show causes.

items.title: Current gaps in downstream applications of fMRI foundation models: lessons learned from BrainLM & BrainHarmonix on Prevent-AD

ai.headline: Two AI brain-scanning models did not reliably predict Alzheimer’s-related outcomes in a new dataset.
ai.summary: Researchers tested two fMRI foundation models, BrainLM and BrainHarmonix, on 343 adults with a family history of Alzheimer’s disease. Neither model beat simple baselines for predicting progression to mild cognitive impairment or amyloid burden, and both needed substantial code changes to run.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that popular AI tools for brain imaging are not yet ready for independent researchers or clinics to use without careful validation.
ai.life_skill: Check whether an AI health tool has been independently tested against simple baselines before trusting its results.
ai.fact: Foundation models that succeed in language and vision cannot yet be assumed to transfer well to fMRI brain-imaging tasks.

quiz.question: Did either foundation model significantly beat the dummy classifier for predicting MCI or amyloid burden?
quiz.answer: No, for both clinical targets no feature exceeded the dummy classifier in accuracy and AUC stayed near chance.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and is a single dataset study, so the findings are not proof that these models generally fail.

items.title: PRACT to Investigate Controlling Alcohol Related Harms in a Low-Income Setting; Emergency Department BIs in Tanzania

ai.summary: Researchers are testing a Swahili-language brief intervention called PPKAY for injury patients at an emergency department in Moshi, Tanzania. It uses adaptive trial methods to find which parts of the intervention work best and how well it reduces alcohol-related harms overall.

items.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents

ai.summary: Researchers studied speculative decoding in long-horizon agents and found that controlling numerical noise improves reasoning accuracy. ai.fact: Speculative decoding can influence the output distribution of a model after multiple steps

quiz.answer: They were associated with higher perceived legitimacy and lower vigilance toward AI-generated health messages.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a single qualitative interview study with two cohorts and two visual styles, so they cannot prove cause and effect or apply to all populations.

items.title: The relationship between Tai Chi exercise and psychological distress in older adults: the chain mediation effect of mood state and sleep quality

ai.headline: Tai Chi exercise is linked to less psychological distress in older adults, partly via better mood and sleep.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 457 older adults about Tai Chi exercise, mood, sleep quality and psychological distress. They found that more Tai Chi was linked to lower distress, and this link was partly explained by better mood and better sleep. Together, mood and sleep accounted for more than half of the total association.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that gentle movement like Tai Chi might support mental wellbeing in later life through mood and sleep, though it does not prove cause and effect.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether gentle movement such as Tai Chi seems to improve your mood and sleep.
ai.fact: Tai Chi exercise is linked to lower psychological distress in older adults, partly through mood state and sleep quality.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest explains part of the link between Tai Chi and lower psychological distress?
quiz.answer: Better mood state and better sleep quality acted as mediators in the relationship.

ai.caveat: This was an observational questionnaire study, so it cannot establish that Tai Chi causes lower psychological distress.

items.title: Patient expectations for artificial intelligence transparency and agency: A qualitative study and proportionate framework for clinical artificial intelligence implementation

ai.headline: Patients want to know when AI is used in their care, with more detail for higher-risk decisions.
ai.summary: This qualitative study interviewed patient advisory council members to understand their views on AI in healthcare. Participants emphasized that transparency is an ethical baseline for trust and that clinicians must remain the final decision-makers, acting as a bridge between the technology and the patient.
ai.why_it_matters: As AI becomes common in daily services, understanding that trust requires clear communication and human oversight helps you navigate new digital tools confidently.
ai.life_skill: Ask clearly how any automated tool influences a decision affecting you, and request a human explanation if the stakes are high.
ai.fact: Patients view transparency as an ethical 'floor' necessary for maintaining autonomy in healthcare.

quiz.question: According to the study, what role do patients expect clinicians to play regarding AI?
quiz.answer: Patients expect clinicians to act as a 'bridge' between the technology and the patient, serving as the final arbiter of care decisions.

ai.caveat: The findings are based on interviews with a specific group of patient advisors and may not represent the views of all patients.

items.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep

ai.headline: Researchers are testing if sound cues during sleep can help Parkinson's patients learn better.
ai.summary: This paper describes the design of a double-blind randomised trial involving 50 people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment. It tests whether adding phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) to digital cognitive training improves executive functions more than training alone.
ai.why_it_matters: It explores a simple, non-invasive way to potentially boost the brain's ability to learn and retain information during sleep.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your sleep quality affects your ability to focus and learn during the day.
ai.fact: Phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) is a technique that uses sound cues to enhance deep sleep.

quiz.question: What is the primary outcome being measured in this trial?
quiz.answer: The primary outcome is executive functions.

ai.caveat: This is a protocol paper describing the study design, so it contains no results or evidence of effectiveness yet.

items.title: Assessing Arab Contributions to Environmental SDGs: Water, Energy, Urban Sustainability and Climate Action

ai.headline: Arab countries show uneven progress on environmental goals, with Gulf states ahead and conflict-affected states behind.
ai.summary: The study compared Arab countries’ progress on environmental SDGs covering water, energy, cities and climate action using national review reports. It found strong progress in renewable energy and urban development, but water management and climate action remain major challenges, with large gaps between Gulf countries and conflict-affected states.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how national wealth and conflict can shape a region’s ability to meet shared environmental goals.
ai.life_skill: Notice how local water and energy choices connect to wider global goals.
ai.fact: The study used a 0–5 scoring framework to compare Arab countries’ environmental SDG performance.

quiz.question: Which two environmental areas showed strong progress according to the study?
quiz.answer: Renewable energy and urban development showed strong progress.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed and relies on secondary national reports.

items.title: Short-Term Effects on Parenting and Adolescent Well-Being of a Personalized Digital Parenting Intervention. A Randomized Controlled Trial

ai.headline: A digital parenting program did not beat daily diary self-monitoring for improving parenting or teen well-being.
ai.summary: A preregistered randomized trial compared 321 families doing 100 daily diaries with 225 families who also received a feedback report and six weeks of online parenting tips. Parents in the control group became less warm and autonomy-supportive, while those in the intervention groups did not show that decline, though no significant differences were found between groups overall.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that simply tracking parenting daily may be as helpful as adding digital tips and feedback for family relationships.
ai.life_skill: Try keeping a short daily record of how you interact with your child to notice patterns over time.
ai.fact: Parents who kept daily diaries reported becoming less warm and autonomy-supportive over the study period.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed.

items.title: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT: Gamifying Fitness with Real-Time Pose Estimation

ai.headline: A smartphone-based VR exergame made HIIT more enjoyable and immersive for young adults, without feeling harder.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a system that uses a smartphone camera and AI pose estimation to track full-body movement during VR high-intensity interval training. In a small within-subject study of 20 people aged 18-25, VR sessions were rated significantly more enjoyable, immersive, and recommendable than non-VR sessions, while perceived intensity stayed similar.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how low-cost technology could make intense exercise feel more engaging, which may help people stick with fitness routines.
ai.life_skill: Try using a phone or app to track your movement during home workouts so you can see your form and stay motivated.
ai.fact: The AI feedback system agreed with a certified trainer’s assessment in 87.5% of the 10 sessions reviewed.

quiz.question: Did participants find the VR HIIT workouts harder than the non-VR ones?
quiz.answer: No, perceived intensity remained comparable between the VR and non-VR conditions.

ai.caveat: This is a small preprint study with only 20 young adult participants and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the results are preliminary and may not apply to other age groups or settings.

items.title: Multi-model forecasting of respiratory disease activity in Germany during the 2024-2025 season

ai.headline: Computer models can track current flu levels well but struggle to predict exactly when winter peaks will hit.
ai.summary: Researchers in Germany tested eight different computer models to predict respiratory disease activity during the 2024-2025 winter. While the models were good at estimating current case numbers, they often failed to predict the exact timing and height of the seasonal peak, frequently guessing the peak would happen earlier than it actually did.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the limits of these predictions helps people and health services plan better for winter, rather than relying on forecasts that might be off by several weeks.
ai.life_skill: Notice that short-term weather or health forecasts are often more accurate than long-term predictions, so plan flexible responses rather than rigid schedules.
ai.fact: Combining multiple forecasting models into an ensemble often improves accuracy, but it does not guarantee better results than using a single strong model.

quiz.question: What was the main weakness of the forecasting models in this study?
quiz.answer: The models often predicted the peak of respiratory disease activity would occur earlier than it actually did.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings are specific to the German surveillance system during one winter season.

items.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation

ai.headline: A new AI method trains image and video generators to work well in just four steps.
ai.summary: The paper studies VA-TDM, a way to improve few-step diffusion and flow models by using velocity fields and a learned critic to guide training. It reports state-of-the-art four-step performance in text-to-image and text-to-video generation, including a 33B model that beats a fast baseline and approaches the quality of slower, many-step generation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI image and video tools can become faster and cheaper to run without losing much quality.
ai.life_skill: Try noticing whether an AI image or video generator offers a fast, few-step mode and compare its quality to the slower setting.
ai.fact: VA-TDM combines velocity adversarial distillation with trajectory distribution matching to improve few-step generators.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its claims are not independently confirmed.

items.title: Gestures that acknowledge I’m here

ai.headline: Small gestures that acknowledge a patient can be remembered for decades after a medical emergency.
ai.summary: This is a personal account from someone admitted to hospital at 16 with a catastrophic gastrointestinal bleed who was not expected to survive. They describe remaining conscious and able to hear while critically ill, and recalling calmness, humour, and being acknowledged by staff nearly 50 years later.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how simple human interactions during serious illness can leave a lasting impression on patients.
ai.life_skill: Notice how small acknowledgements affect people around you, especially when they are vulnerable.
ai.fact: A patient can hear and understand what is happening around them even when they cannot speak or move much during a medical emergency.

quiz.question: What did the author remember nearly 50 years after being critically ill in hospital?
quiz.answer: They remembered calmness, humour, and being acknowledged by staff.

ai.caveat: This is a single personal account, not a study of many patients, so it cannot show how common these experiences are.

items.title: Centuries-old cemetery helps scientists link climate shocks to Industrial Revolution disease

ai.headline: Climate shocks may have helped drive rickets during England's Industrial Revolution.
ai.summary: Researchers used a centuries-old cemetery to study disease during England's Industrial Revolution. They found that climate, alongside urbanisation, latitude and socioeconomic status, may have contributed to rickets in children.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how environmental conditions can shape health during major economic change.
ai.life_skill: Notice how weather and sunlight affect your own health and wellbeing.
ai.fact: Rickets is a condition in which the growing skeleton fails to properly mineralize.

quiz.question: What overlooked factor did researchers suggest may have driven rickets during the Industrial Revolution?
quiz.answer: Climate may have been an overlooked driver of rickets alongside urbanisation, latitude and socioeconomic status.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about research, not the study itself, so the findings cannot be treated as proven.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints

ai.headline: AI can help design germ-killing peptides that avoid harming human blood cells.
ai.summary: Researchers adapted a protein language model to predict both antibacterial strength and toxicity to human red blood cells at the same time. The model found new peptide candidates with high therapeutic potential while filtering out broadly destructive ones.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how artificial intelligence could speed up the search for new treatments as antibiotic resistance grows.
ai.life_skill: Notice how new medicines are discovered and check reliable health sources before trusting claims about new treatments.
ai.fact: Antimicrobial peptides can kill bacteria by disrupting membranes but may also damage human red blood cells.

quiz.question: What two properties did the AI model try to predict at once?
quiz.answer: It predicted antibacterial potency and hemolytic toxicity against mammalian red blood cells.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the results come from computer screening rather than tests in people.

items.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics

ai.headline: Ancient DNA from thousands of Europeans is being used to test how Celtic languages spread.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to see whether demographic history supports different theories about the origin and spread of Celtic languages.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how genetics can help explain how languages and cultures moved across Europe in the distant past.
ai.fact: Genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals were analysed to test models for the origin and spread of Celtic languages.

quiz.question: What did researchers analyse to test theories about Celtic languages?
quiz.answer: They analysed genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe.

ai.caveat: The abstract reports the study design and data but not its findings, so no conclusions about Celtic language spread can be drawn yet.

items.title: Pediatricians see vaping risks, but lack tools to help teens quit

ai.headline: Most Australian pediatricians don't know where to refer teens who want to quit vaping.
ai.summary: Federation University research surveyed Australian pediatricians about adolescent vaping. It found that two-thirds do not know where to refer adolescents for support to quit vaping.
ai.why_it_matters: This shows a gap in healthcare support that could leave young people trying to quit vaping without professional help.
ai.life_skill: Ask a trusted health professional where to find local support for quitting vaping.
ai.fact: Two-thirds of Australian pediatricians surveyed did not know where to refer adolescents for vaping cessation support.

quiz.question: What proportion of Australian pediatricians did not know where to refer adolescents for vaping quit support?
quiz.answer: Two-thirds did not know where to refer adolescents for support to quit vaping.

ai.caveat: This is based on a news report of a single study, so the findings are not yet established proof.

items.title: A tiny squeeze dramatically changes the magnetism of exotic materials

ai.headline: Squeezing exotic materials called altermagnets can change their magnetism and electrical behavior.
ai.summary: Scientists studied altermagnets, a type of exotic material. They found that applying a simple mechanical squeeze dramatically alters their magnetic properties and electrical behavior.
ai.why_it_matters: This could lead to faster, more energy-efficient electronics and new quantum computing technologies.
ai.fact: Mechanical pressure can change the magnetic and electrical properties of altermagnets.

quiz.question: What effect did squeezing have on altermagnets?
quiz.answer: It dramatically altered their magnetic properties and electrical behavior.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original peer-reviewed research, so the findings are not yet independently verified.

items.title: Manufacturing Renaissance Meets Time-Inconsistent Tariffs -- by Christoph Boehm, Andrei A. Levchenko, Wei Xiang

ai.headline: Governments may promise future tariffs to boost local factories, but often drop them when prices rise.
ai.summary: The study uses an economic model where creating new firms takes time. It finds that policymakers might announce future tariffs to encourage domestic manufacturing, but face a temptation to avoid immediate tariffs because they raise consumer prices right away.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why promises about future trade protection can be hard to believe and how that affects whether local manufacturing grows.
ai.life_skill: Notice when a policy promises future benefits but imposes immediate costs, and check whether the promise is backed by a binding commitment.
ai.fact: Time-inconsistency means a policymaker’s preferred plan today can differ from what they want to do later.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a theoretical model, not peer-reviewed evidence from real-world data.

items.title: U.S. archaeology faces ‘apocalyptic’ threat

ai.headline: Proposed changes to US law could weaken reviews that protect archaeological sites before projects begin.
ai.summary: A news report from Science describes moves by Congress and the White House to weaken a key law requiring pre-project reviews. The report frames this as an apocalyptic threat to US archaeology.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how government decisions can affect whether physical traces of the past are preserved or lost.
ai.life_skill: Notice how local planning decisions can affect heritage sites in your area.
ai.fact: US law currently requires reviews before many projects to consider effects on archaeological sites.

quiz.question: What does the key US law described in the report require before projects?
quiz.answer: It requires pre-project reviews to consider effects on archaeological sites.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a research study, so it does not provide evidence of effects or outcomes.

items.title: Cognitive-behavioral therapy in people with Parkinson's disease and caregivers: A mixed method systematic review on clinical applications and therapeutic outcomes

ai.headline: CBT may help depression in people with Parkinson’s disease, but evidence for other symptoms is weak.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 54 studies looked at cognitive behavioural therapy for people with Parkinson’s disease and their caregivers. Moderate-certainty evidence supports CBT for depression, while evidence for anxiety, sleep, impulse control, cognition, motor symptoms and caregiver outcomes is limited or very uncertain.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows which non-motor symptoms of Parkinson’s have stronger psychological support and where more research is still needed.
ai.life_skill: Talk to a qualified healthcare professional about whether CBT could be suitable for managing low mood related to Parkinson’s disease.
ai.fact: Moderate-certainty evidence from several randomised trials supports CBT for depression in people with Parkinson’s disease.

quiz.question: For which symptom does the review report moderate-certainty evidence that CBT is effective?
quiz.answer: Depression.

ai.caveat: The review includes studies of varying design and quality, and evidence for most outcomes beyond depression is low or very low certainty.

items.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Dietary and Physical Activity Behaviours Among Adolescents: A Systematic Review
items.venue: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics

ai.headline: Teenagers from wealthier backgrounds tend to eat healthier diets and join more organised physical activities.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 38 studies on how socioeconomic position relates to adolescents' eating and activity habits. It found that higher socioeconomic position was linked to healthier diets, more fruit and vegetables, and more organised physical activity, while lower socioeconomic position was linked to poorer diet quality, skipping breakfast, and eating more ultra-processed foods.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a young person's eating and activity habits are shaped by their family's social and economic circumstances, not just personal choice.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your local food options and activity opportunities might differ from those in other neighbourhoods.
ai.fact: Parental education was the socioeconomic indicator most consistently linked to adolescents' dietary behaviours.

quiz.question: Which behaviour showed inconsistent links to socioeconomic position according to the review?
quiz.answer: Associations with total physical activity and sedentary behaviour were inconsistent.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were observational, so they show links rather than prove that socioeconomic position causes these behaviours.

items.title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

ai.headline: Home-based exercise improves heart and lung fitness in cancer survivors treated with cardiotoxic therapies.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at ten randomised trials involving 851 cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic treatments. Home-based exercise programmes significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak), but did not significantly improve six-minute walk distance or quality of life, and evidence on direct heart damage markers was limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercising at home may help cancer survivors maintain fitness after heart-harming treatments, though it cannot yet be said to prevent heart damage.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular home-based movement into your routine if you are recovering from cancer treatment, after checking with your care team.
ai.fact: Home-based exercise significantly improved VO2 peak by 2.35 mL/kg/min in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies.

quiz.question: What did home-based exercise significantly improve in cancer survivors according to the review?
quiz.answer: It significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness, measured as VO2 peak.

ai.caveat: The review is based on ten trials and direct heart damage outcomes were assessed in only one study, so firm conclusions about preventing heart toxicity cannot be drawn.

items.title: Family factors and school refusal among children and adolescents: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis

ai.headline: Family difficulties are modestly linked to school refusal in children and teenagers.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis combined results from studies on family factors and school refusal among children and adolescents. It found that greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal, though the strength of this link varied widely across studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that family context can matter when understanding why a young person avoids school, without proving that family problems cause the refusal.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether family stress or support patterns line up with school avoidance, and consider speaking with a trusted adult or professional if it persists.
ai.fact: Family risk and protection factors are associated with school refusal, but the evidence does not establish cause and effect.

quiz.question: What did the review find about family factors and school refusal?
quiz.answer: Greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mostly observational, so it cannot show whether family difficulties cause school refusal or result from it.

items.title: How Much Active Learning? A Rapid Systematic Review of Contextual Moderators and an Evidence-Weighted Dosage Model for Political Science Teaching

ai.headline: Active learning boosts grades, but more isn't always better once you pass a moderate level.
ai.summary: A rapid review of 58 studies looked at how much active learning university courses should use. It found that mid- and high-intensity active learning bring similar grade gains, both well above low intensity, while closing achievement gaps seems to need high intensity. Effects are larger in small classes.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps students and teachers understand how to balance active learning with other teaching without assuming more is always better.
ai.life_skill: Try mixing active tasks like discussion or problem-solving into about half your study time rather than only listening or reading.
ai.fact: Meta-analyses link active learning in higher education to achievement gains of about half a standard deviation.

quiz.question: What did the review find about mid- versus high-intensity active learning?
quiz.answer: They produce similar achievement gains, both far above low intensity.

ai.caveat: It is a preprint not yet peer reviewed and a rapid review, so the evidence is not definitive.

items.title: Variation in recommendations for management of pediatric fever and neutropenia across databases and languages: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines

ai.headline: Guidelines for children's fever with low white blood cells vary by language and database searched.
ai.summary: Researchers reviewed 14 clinical practice guidelines on managing fever with neutropenia in children. They found each database contained one unique guideline, only 36% were indexed in all three databases, and agreement with a reference guideline ranged from 33% to 100%.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that where and in what language clinicians look for guidance can change the advice they find, affecting care worldwide.
ai.life_skill: Check several trusted sources and languages when looking up health guidance rather than relying on one database.
ai.fact: Fever with neutropenia is a common complication of cancer therapy in children linked to serious illness, death, and high resource use.

quiz.question: What percentage of the 14 guidelines were indexed in all three databases?
quiz.answer: Only 36% (5 out of 14) were indexed in all three databases.

ai.caveat: The review included only 14 guidelines from the last 10 years and did not prove that database or language restrictions directly cause worse patient outcomes.

items.title: Dyslexia extends beyond reading difficulties: genetic links with social functioning and well-being

ai.headline: Genetic liability to dyslexia is linked to lower life satisfaction, loneliness, and less workplace support.
ai.summary: Researchers combined genetic and survey data from the Lifelines cohort with public genome-wide study results to examine links between dyslexia and social traits. They found that dyslexia was associated with lower life satisfaction, higher loneliness, and less collegial support at work, and that genetic liability to dyslexia predicted increased loneliness and social isolation.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that dyslexia may affect social and emotional wellbeing beyond reading and spelling, suggesting a need for broader support throughout life.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether reading difficulties are affecting your social confidence or sense of connection, and consider speaking with a trusted adult or professional about support.
ai.fact: Dyslexia is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterised by persistent difficulties in reading and spelling.

quiz.question: What did the study find about the direction of the relationship between dyslexia and social outcomes?
quiz.answer: The evidence pointed from dyslexia toward adverse social and wellbeing outcomes, not the other way around.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it is observational, so it cannot prove causation on its own.

items.title: Convergent genome- and gene-level constraints shape repeated environmental adaptation in grasses

ai.headline: Grasses adapt to extreme environments through predictable genetic changes across many species.
ai.summary: The study examined 687 grass genomes from 561 species across 17 climate zones. It found that grasses repeatedly shift similar genome-wide properties and use the same genes when adapting to extreme temperature, water, and soil conditions.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how plants survive harsh conditions, which matters for food security and ecosystems.
ai.fact: Grasses show repeated, predictable genetic changes when adapting to extreme environments.

quiz.question: What did researchers find about how grasses adapt to extreme environments?
quiz.answer: Grasses repeatedly use similar genetic changes across many species when adapting to extreme temperature, water, and soil conditions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Factors Associated with Meaning in Life Among Hispanic Adults in the Post-Pandemic Period: A Cross-Sectional Study Across 16 Countries

ai.headline: About half of Hispanic adults across 16 countries reported low meaning in life after the pandemic.
ai.summary: A cross-sectional study of 10,142 Hispanic adults aged 18 to 78 across 16 countries examined meaning in life after the pandemic. It found that 50.2% had low meaning in life, while mental health, occupational purpose, gratitude, friendships, and meaningful activities were linked to higher meaning, and low perceived workplace success, lack of gratitude, and heavy social media use were linked to lower meaning.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling a sense of meaning may depend more on everyday habits and relationships than on income or education.
ai.life_skill: Notice which activities and friendships make your life feel meaningful and make time for them regularly.
ai.fact: In this study, income, education, and gender were not significantly associated with meaning in life.

quiz.question: What percentage of participants experienced low levels of meaning in life?
quiz.answer: 50.2% of participants experienced low levels of meaning in life.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and because it is cross-sectional it cannot show that the linked factors actually cause changes in meaning in life.

items.title: AI may help tailor treatment for childhood brain tumors

ai.headline: An AI model may help doctors choose more precise treatments for children with malignant brain tumors.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an artificial intelligence model to help balance effective cancer treatment with avoiding lasting side effects on learning, development and quality of life. The model may support doctors in making treatment decisions with greater precision.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could one day improve care for children with serious illnesses by weighing treatment benefits against long-term harms.

quiz.question: What did the researchers develop to help with childhood brain tumor treatment decisions?
quiz.answer: They developed an artificial intelligence model that may help doctors make those decisions with greater precision.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a model that may help; it is not peer-reviewed evidence that the model works in practice.

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence

ai.headline: Researchers propose AI companions that stay with a person lifelong to extend human thinking and memory.
ai.summary: This is a theory paper, not a study with data. It argues that AI should move beyond autonomous agents to become embedded, lifelong “cognitive symbionts” that sense a person’s context, remember their history, and think alongside them to close the gap between what people could know and what working memory can hold.

ai.life_skill: Notice when you forget something useful and consider whether a trusted digital tool could help you capture it for later.
ai.fact: The paper introduces “AI-augmented human intelligence” as the idea of measuring how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person.

quiz.question: What does the paper call an AI system that stays with a person lifelong and thinks alongside them?
quiz.answer: It calls it a cognitive symbiont.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint theory paper with no data or experiments, so the ideas are untested proposals rather than proven findings.

items.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval

ai.headline: A new AI method improves image search by imagining how to change a picture before matching it.
ai.summary: The paper studies composed image retrieval, where a user finds a target image using a reference image plus a text description of changes. It introduces FactEmbed, which separates understanding the requested visual change from creating a search-friendly image representation, and reports better results than earlier methods on retrieval benchmarks.

ai.fact: FactEmbed uses factorized latents to simulate intended visual modifications before forming discriminative embeddings for retrieval.

quiz.question: What does FactEmbed do before forming a search-friendly image representation?
quiz.answer: It uses factorized latents to simulate the intended visual modifications and ground into target semantics.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, so its claims are not yet independently confirmed.

items.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries

ai.headline: Preprimary education eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes and greater reproductive autonomy for women across 117 low- and middle-income countries.
ai.summary: The study looked at eligibility for preprimary education in 117 low- and middle-income countries. It found that eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how early childhood education policies may be connected to women’s opportunities and life choices around the world.
ai.life_skill: Notice how access to early education can shape opportunities for girls and women in your community.
ai.fact: Preprimary education eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes and greater reproductive autonomy for women across 117 low- and middle-income countries.

quiz.question: What did the study find is linked to eligibility for preprimary education across 117 low- and middle-income countries?
quiz.answer: Eligibility is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing.

ai.caveat: The findings show a link, not proof that preprimary education causes these changes, because the study is observational.

items.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial

ai.headline: A small trial tested ivonescimab alone or with chemotherapy before lung cancer surgery and found promising responses in both groups.
ai.summary: In a nonrandomised phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received ivonescimab either alone or with chemotherapy around the time of surgery. Both groups showed encouraging pathological response rates, and sustained circulating tumour DNA negativity during neoadjuvant therapy may predict response.
