It found that sumud is enacted through family, intergenerational stories, cultural practices, and institutions, supporting meaning-making and identity continuity, while also creating burdens for women, caregivers, and professionals.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that mental health support can work better when it accounts for a person’s cultural background, relationships, and community rather than only individual traits.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your family, community, and cultural traditions help you cope during difficult times.
ai.fact: Sumud is an Arabic concept of steadfastness and endurance that functions as a collective, culturally embedded form of resilience.

quiz.question: What did the review find that sumud supports?
quiz.answer: Sumud supports meaning-making, emotional regulation, and identity continuity.

ai.caveat: The review combines varied study types and notes that sumud-informed psychotherapeutic interventions remain scarce and not yet rigorously evaluated.

items.title: Structural associations between psychosocial risks and burnout syndrome among mining workers in Peru

ai.headline: Some mining-work stressors link to burnout, while active work and skill development link to less burnout.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 260 mining workers in Peru using questionnaires on psychosocial risks and burnout. Higher psychological demands were linked to greater emotional exhaustion, while active work and skill development were linked to lower emotional exhaustion and depersonalization.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace conditions may relate to burnout, helping people recognise which job factors could affect wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your job lets you use and develop your skills, and consider discussing workload or support with your employer.
ai.fact: Burnout includes emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, and reduced personal accomplishment.
ai.caveat: The data were collected at one time and cannot show whether psychosocial risks cause burnout.

items.title: Staff retention in echocardiography: a formal exploration of workforce drivers

ai.headline: NHS echocardiography staff are more likely to consider leaving if they are younger, overworked, or lack career progression.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed and held discussions with 45 echocardiography staff at one NHS Trust. Most team leaders planned to stay, while about 39% of frontline Band 7 staff said they might leave within two years; supportive management, good relationships, flexibility and work-life balance helped retention, while workload, burnout and limited progression drove people away.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that keeping skilled healthcare workers depends on more than pay, including team support and manageable workloads.
ai.life_skill: Notice what makes you want to stay in a job and discuss flexibility or workload concerns with your manager.
ai.fact: Supportive management, positive team relationships, flexibility and work-life balance are linked to echocardiography staff wanting to stay in their roles.

quiz.question: What share of Band 7 echocardiographers said they might leave within two years?
quiz.answer: 39% of Band 7 staff indicated potential intention to leave within two years.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a small service evaluation at a single NHS Trust, so they may not apply to all echocardiography staff or settings.

items.title: Network structure of non-suicidal self-injury and multidomain psychiatric symptoms among adolescents with elevated depressive symptoms: a cross-sectional study

ai.headline: Self-injury in teens with low mood is linked to anxiety, trauma, and obsessive symptoms, not just depression.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 1,146 school-based adolescents with elevated depressive symptoms to map how non-suicidal self-injury connects with other mental-health symptoms. Self-injury belonged to a core group with depression, trauma, obsessive-compulsive, and general anxiety symptoms, while separation, social, and school anxiety formed a separate group.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that assessing anxiety, trauma, and intrusive-thought symptoms alongside low mood may give a fuller picture of a teenager's distress.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether low mood comes with other worries, intrusive thoughts, or difficult memories, and speak to a trusted adult or professional about it.
ai.fact: Non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents with elevated depressive symptoms is associated with depression, trauma-related, obsessive-compulsive, and general anxiety symptoms, not only mood-related distress.

quiz.question: Which symptom domains were most closely linked with non-suicidal self-injury in this study?
quiz.answer: Depressive, trauma-related, obsessive-compulsive, and general anxiety symptoms were most closely linked with it.

ai.caveat: The study was a cross-sectional preprint, so it shows descriptive links only and cannot establish cause and effect.

items.title: Age‐Related Patterns of Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) Symptoms and Key Performance Factors in Adolescent Biathletes

ai.headline: RED symptoms are common in young biathletes and linked to poorer race performance.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 72 adolescent biathletes to see how common REDs symptoms were and how they related to end-of-season race results. About a third showed REDs symptoms, and illness or injury-related training absences were linked to poorer performance. Symptoms were more common in females and older athletes.
ai.why_it_matters: Spotting under-fuelling early in teenage athletes may help protect both their health and their sporting futures.
ai.life_skill: Tell a coach or health professional if you often feel tired, injured, or miss training.
ai.fact: About one in three adolescent biathletes in the study showed symptoms of REDs.

quiz.question: What was linked to poorer end-of-season race results?
quiz.answer: Illness or injury-related training absences were linked to poorer performance.

ai.caveat: Because the study was observational, it cannot prove that REDs symptoms caused the poorer race results.

items.title: Covering all the BASEs? Barriers and facilitators to STI testing among international students living in England

ai.headline: International students in England face stigma, language, and service barriers to STI testing.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 15 international students at a London university about sexually transmitted infection testing. They found that language gaps, stigma, and distant services made testing harder, while confidentiality, trust in professionals, and knowing about free, easy testing made it easier.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding these barriers helps universities and health services design better sexual health support for students from diverse backgrounds.
ai.life_skill: Find out where free, confidential STI testing is available near your university or home.
ai.fact: Confidentiality and trust in health professionals can encourage people to get tested for sexually transmitted infections.

quiz.question: What did the researchers identify as the main social barrier to STI testing among the students interviewed?
quiz.answer: Anticipated judgement and stigma were the main social opportunity barriers to testing.

ai.caveat: This is a small preprint from one London university that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the results may not apply more widely.

items.title: Modular functional brain network organization contributes to training-related changes in task switching in children

ai.headline: Children with more modular brain networks before training improved faster at task switching.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 87 children aged 8 to 11 during nine weeks of task-switching training. More modular brain networks before training were linked to higher accuracy and faster early gains in combined speed-accuracy scores.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that baseline brain network organisation may help explain why some people benefit more from cognitive training than others.
ai.fact: More modular organisation of functional brain networks before training was linked to higher task-switching accuracy and faster early improvement in children aged 8 to 11.

quiz.question: What was linked to faster early improvements in children's task-switching training?
quiz.answer: More modular organisation of functional brain networks before training was linked to faster early improvements.

ai.caveat: The findings are from a single preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the observational design cannot prove that modularity causes the faster improvement.

items.title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality

ai.headline: AI hiring tools may reject good candidates simply because they used a different AI to write their cover letter.
ai.summary: This preprint tested how AI evaluators rate job applications written by various AI models. It found that evaluators consistently favour applications from specific models and their own outputs, regardless of the candidate's actual qualifications.
ai.why_it_matters: If you use AI to help with job applications, the specific tool you choose could unfairly disadvantage you compared to others using different tools.
ai.life_skill: Check if your employer uses AI screening and consider how your choice of writing tool might affect the outcome.
ai.fact: AI evaluators show a consistent preference hierarchy for certain writer models, often favouring their own outputs over others.

quiz.question: Did the study find that AI evaluators judged candidates based on their actual qualifications?
quiz.answer: No, the study found that evaluators favoured specific AI models and their own outputs independently of candidate quality.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings are not yet confirmed by the scientific community.

items.title: HOW GUT MICROBIOTA MAY MEDIATE THE ANTI-SEIZURE EFFECTS OF KETOGENIC DIET IN PEDIATRIC DRUG-RESISTANT EPILEPSY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW

ai.headline: Gut bacteria may help the ketogenic diet reduce seizures in children with drug-resistant epilepsy.
ai.summary: This narrative review examines how the ketogenic diet (KD) works for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy. It suggests that beyond ketones, specific gut bacteria produce chemicals that calm brain activity, similar to how some seizure medications work.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that what we eat can change our gut bacteria, which in turn can influence how our brain functions and responds to treatment.
ai.life_skill: Notice that your diet can influence your gut health, which is linked to overall well-being.
ai.fact: Specific gut bacteria, such as Akkermansia muciniphila, are required for the ketogenic diet to effectively reduce seizures in animal models.

quiz.question: According to the review, how might gut bacteria help the ketogenic diet work?
quiz.answer: They produce short-chain fatty acids that modulate the balance of GABA and glutamate in the hippocampus.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and the mechanistic evidence for the gut-brain link is primarily from preclinical (animal) studies rather than direct human trials.

items.title: The Workings of Social Fields: Poverty, Capital, and Symbolic Violence across Five Domains

ai.headline: Having useful skills and qualifications does not guarantee a livelihood because others control how they are valued and used.
ai.summary: The paper compares six analyses of Dutch interviews across employment, welfare, informal exchange, neighbourhood relations and debt management. It finds that recognition of a resource can coexist with blocked access, and that people may keep only part of what a resource produces because control over valuation, access and benefits is split between different actors.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows why immediate help, personal freedom and lasting financial improvement are different things that should not be confused when tackling poverty.
ai.life_skill: Notice who decides whether your skills or connections actually count in a given situation, not just whether they are recognised.
ai.fact: Recognition of a skill or resource can exist at the same time as blocked access to using it.

quiz.question: What can coexist with blocked access to a resource, according to the paper?
quiz.answer: Recognition of the resource can coexist with blocked access to using it.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and synthesises existing interview analyses rather than presenting new evidence.

items.title: Saving for the Machines -- by Jesús Fernández-Villaverde

ai.headline: Automation growth depends on capital accumulation
ai.summary: The study examined how automation affects economic growth, finding that capital accumulation plays a crucial role in determining the size of the growth boom. The research used a standard task model to analyze the impact of automation on growth and wages. The results showed that a fixed saving rate can lead to slower growth, while an optimal saving rate can deliver higher growth rates.
ai.why_it_matters: This research matters because it suggests that slow economic growth might be due to insufficient capital accumulation rather than a technological bottleneck, which has implications for economic policy and decision-making.
ai.life_skill: Try to understand the importance of saving and investing in a rapidly changing technological landscape.
ai.fact: The same technology path can deliver different growth rates depending on the saving rate.

quiz.question: What can affect the size of the growth boom associated with automation?
quiz.answer: Capital accumulation can affect the size of the growth boom associated with automation.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Reducing Stroke Risk in African-American Men

ai.headline: A six-month trial tested a targeted management intervention for African-American men after stroke or TIA.
ai.summary: The study compared a TEAM intervention with a wait-list control in 160 African-American men who had a stroke or transient ischaemic attack in the past five years. It was a randomised controlled trial, but the abstract does not report what the intervention involved or what results were found.
ai.why_it_matters: Stroke prevention matters because it can reduce serious illness and death in a group known to face higher stroke risk.

quiz.question: What type of study compared TEAM with a wait-list control?
quiz.answer: It was a six-month prospective randomised controlled trial.

ai.caveat: The abstract gives no results, so it is not possible to say whether the intervention worked.

items.title: Restricting candy may increase kids' urge to overeat, research suggests

ai.headline: Restricting candy may increase children's urge to overeat it, research suggests.
ai.summary: The article discusses research suggesting that restricting candy may increase children's urge to overeat it. It focuses on how parents handle negotiations around candy consumption after holidays and events.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights how common parenting approaches to sweets might unintentionally affect children's eating behaviour.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether restricting certain foods makes you or others want them more.
ai.fact: Restricting candy may increase children's urge to overeat it.

quiz.question: What does the research suggest happens when candy is restricted?
quiz.answer: It may increase children's urge to overeat it.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not the original research, so the study design and findings cannot be verified from the abstract alone.

items.title: Five overlooked steps to identify new epidemics, fast

ai.headline: Current epidemic tracking fails when diseases cause unusual or unexpected symptoms.
ai.summary: This commentary highlights a major limitation in current measures for tracking emerging epidemics. It notes that these systems do not work effectively if a disease presents with unusual or unexpected symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding this gap helps explain why some new health threats might be missed or delayed in detection by public health systems.
ai.life_skill: Notice that standard health alerts might miss diseases with unusual symptoms, so stay open to new information from official sources.
ai.fact: Current epidemic tracking measures have a key limitation regarding diseases with unusual or unexpected symptoms.

quiz.question: What is a key limitation of current epidemic tracking measures mentioned in the text?
quiz.answer: They don’t work if the disease causes unusual or unexpected symptoms.

ai.caveat: This is a commentary identifying a limitation, not a study providing new data or testing a solution.

items.title: [World Report] Health-care costs could help decide US midterm elections

ai.headline: US health-care costs may influence the outcome of the midterm elections.
ai.summary: This news report describes how Democrats hope to win voters by focusing on cuts to health-care programmes ahead of the US midterm elections.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how health-care spending can become a major political issue that affects everyday voters.
ai.life_skill: Check how political parties plan to fund health-care programmes before voting.
ai.fact: Democrats hope to win voters’ support by focusing on cuts to health-care programmes.

quiz.question: What do Democrats hope to focus on to win voters’ support?
quiz.answer: They hope to focus on cuts to health-care programmes.

ai.caveat: This is a news report, not a research study, so it reports political strategy rather than proven findings.

items.title: Collective human metabolism produces 2 billion metric tons of CO₂ a year, global study estimates

ai.headline: Human breathing released an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons of CO₂ in 2015, up 74% since 1985.
ai.summary: Researchers estimated the carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism as bodies convert food into energy. They found it rose by 74% between 1985 and 2015, reaching 2.05 billion metric tons a year.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how human activity fits into the global carbon cycle and where carbon comes from and goes.
ai.life_skill: Notice how everyday activities like eating and moving connect to the wider environment.
ai.fact: Human metabolism produced an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons of CO₂ in 2015.

quiz.question: By what percentage did CO₂ from human metabolism rise between 1985 and 2015?
quiz.answer: It rose by 74%.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about an estimate, not the full peer-reviewed study, so the figures and methods cannot be checked here.

items.title: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F

ai.headline: Some metals stay flexible at ultra-low temperatures by reorganising their internal structure instead of cracking.
ai.summary: Researchers studied two experimental alloys at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F), where similar materials usually become dangerously brittle. Instead of breaking, the alloys reorganised their internal structures, creating new ways to absorb stress and remain flexible.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how materials might behave in extreme cold, which could matter for future technologies such as space exploration or cryogenic engineering.
ai.fact: Certain alloys can reorganise their internal structure to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F).

quiz.question: What did the two experimental alloys do at -253°C instead of cracking?
quiz.answer: They reorganised their internal structures to absorb stress and remain flexible.

ai.caveat: This is a news report of a discovery, not a peer-reviewed study, so the details and claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Outcomes and organ protection effects of perioperative precision venous access management strategies in patients undergoing complex hepatobiliary, pancreatic, splenic and abdominal great vascular surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

ai.headline: Precision venous access management may reduce kidney injury and pancreatic fistula after major abdominal surgery.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis combined 14 studies with 2,158 adults undergoing complex liver, pancreas, spleen, or major blood vessel surgery. It found that precision venous access management—using advanced monitoring, algorithm-guided therapy, and specialised access—was linked to lower rates of acute kidney injury and clinically relevant pancreatic fistula, fewer overall complications, and shorter hospital stays compared with standard care.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how tailored fluid and monitoring strategies during high-risk surgery might help protect organs and support recovery.
ai.life_skill: Ask your surgical team how your fluids and circulation will be monitored before and after major surgery.
ai.fact: The review included randomised controlled trials and prospective cohort studies comparing precision venous access management with standard treatment.

quiz.question: What did the review find about precision venous access management and acute kidney injury?
quiz.answer: It was linked to a significantly lower incidence of acute kidney injury compared with standard care.

ai.caveat: The included studies varied in design and some were prospective cohorts rather than randomised trials, so the results show a link rather than definitive proof.

items.title: Organizational trust in the workplace: explainable machine learning evidence from Ecuadorian workers

ai.headline: Job satisfaction, cynicism and workplace climate help predict high trust among Ecuadorian workers.
ai.summary: Researchers surveyed 899 workers in Ecuador about trust in their supervisor and organisation, along with cynicism, climate, satisfaction and personal characteristics. Machine-learning models found satisfaction, cynicism and climate were the most useful predictors, though job satisfaction alone performed almost as well as the full set.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace feelings and environment are linked to whether employees trust their organisation, which can affect daily working life.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you feel satisfied with your job, cynical about your organisation, and positive about your workplace climate, as these are linked to trust.
ai.fact: In this study, high organisational trust was defined as a mean score of at least 5.0 on a 12-item inventory measuring trust in the immediate supervisor and the organisation.

quiz.question: Which predictor group performed almost as well as the combined set of satisfaction, cynicism and climate?
quiz.answer: Job satisfaction alone reached a mean nested ROC-AUC of 0.843, close to the combined framework’s 0.875.

ai.caveat: This was a non-experimental cross-sectional survey using a convenience sample from Ecuador, so it shows links rather than proof of cause and effect and may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Exchange Of Instrumental Support Between Grandparents And Grandchildren In Sengerema District, Tanzania
items.venue: International journal of social sciences and humanities review

ai.headline: Grandparents and grandchildren in Tanzania help each other with daily tasks in a flexible, changing way.
ai.summary: A small qualitative study in Sengerema District, Tanzania, explored practical support exchanged between grandparents and grandchildren through interviews, focus groups and observation. Grandparents provided food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education costs, money, supervision and personal care, while grandchildren helped with farming, fetching water, cooking, cleaning, washing, animal care, errands and physically demanding tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how different generations can share everyday responsibilities to keep households running and support family wellbeing.
ai.life_skill: Notice what practical help you give and receive from older or younger family members, and appreciate that it can change over time.
ai.fact: Instrumental support between grandparents and grandchildren can include basic needs, farming, financial help, childcare and household chores.

quiz.question: What kind of support did grandparents and grandchildren exchange in the study?
quiz.answer: They exchanged practical, material and everyday household help such as food, farming, childcare, cooking, cleaning and errands.

ai.caveat: The findings come from a very small number of participants in one Tanzanian district, so they may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Modeling the Psychosocial Determinants of Problematic Social Media Use Risk Among High School Students Using Artificial Neural Networks

ai.headline: Academic expectation stress was the strongest predictor of problematic social media use risk among high school students in this model.
ai.summary: Researchers used an artificial neural network and logistic regression to study 899 high school students, looking at academic expectation stress, loneliness, mobile device ownership, and physical activity as predictors of problematic social media use risk. Academic expectation stress had the highest predictive importance, followed by loneliness, mobile device ownership, and physical activity level.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights which psychosocial factors may be most closely linked to problematic social media use risk in adolescents, helping to understand where support might be focused.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether school-related pressure coincides with increased social media use, and consider talking to a trusted adult or counsellor if it feels hard to manage.
ai.fact: Academic expectation stress had the highest normalized importance (100%) among the four factors studied for predicting problematic social media use risk.

quiz.question: Which factor had the highest normalized importance in predicting problematic social media use risk?
quiz.answer: Academic expectation stress had the highest normalized importance at 100%.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the findings come from a single observational dataset, so they cannot prove causation.

items.title: The consequences of changes in exercise habits on work engagement and presenteeism: Evidence from an event-study analysis using Japanese longitudinal data
items.venue: Scandinavian Journal of Work, Environment & Health

ai.headline: Starting exercise is linked to higher work engagement, while quitting is linked to lower engagement; neither is linked to presenteeism.
ai.summary: Researchers followed over 6,500 Japanese employees across four survey waves to see how starting or stopping exercise habits related to work engagement and presenteeism. Starting exercise was positively associated with work engagement, while quitting was negatively associated with it. Neither starting nor quitting exercise showed a significant association with presenteeism.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that building an exercise habit may support psychological engagement at work, even if it does not clearly improve measured productivity.
ai.life_skill: Try keeping a regular exercise habit rather than focusing only on starting one, since stopping was linked to lower work engagement.
ai.fact: Starting exercise was associated with work engagement over longer follow-up waves than quitting exercise.

quiz.question: What was the association between starting exercise and presenteeism according to the study?
quiz.answer: Starting exercise showed no significant association with presenteeism.

ai.caveat: As an observational study using self-reported survey data, it cannot prove that exercise caused changes in work engagement.

items.title: Prevalence and Sociodemographic Correlates of Depression and Thoughts of Self-Harm Among Adolescents in Five Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Evidence from the Demographic and Health Survey Program

ai.headline: About one in fourteen adolescents in five low- and middle-income countries reported thoughts of death or self-harm, with girls more affected than boys.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed survey data from 16,269 adolescents aged 15-19 in Bangladesh, Lesotho, Mozambique, Nepal and Zambia. Probable depression affected 3.9%, while thoughts of death or self-harm affected 7.0%; girls had higher rates than boys for both.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that thoughts of death or self-harm are not rare among adolescents in these settings, especially girls, so families and communities should be alert to signs of distress.
ai.life_skill: Notice if a friend or family member seems withdrawn, hopeless or talks about death, and encourage them to speak with a trusted adult or a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: In this study, probable depression was defined as a PHQ-9 score of 10 or higher, and thoughts of death or self-harm as any endorsement of PHQ-9 item 9.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and its cross-sectional design cannot show causes; PHQ-9 validation and measurement invariance across countries were also lacking.

items.title: DCAF: Unifying Data Validity, Evaluation Validity and Predictive Modeling for Single-cell Perturbation Simulation

ai.headline: A new computer framework improves predictions of how single cells respond to genetic changes.
ai.summary: The study introduces DCAF, a framework that reconstructs cell states before and after genetic perturbation, evaluates prediction errors more sensitively, and models gene regulation. It outperformed existing deep-learning and simple baseline methods across several tests, including adult mouse brain data.
ai.why_it_matters: Better cell-response simulations could speed up understanding of disease and the discovery of new treatments.
ai.fact: DCAF is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed.

quiz.question: What does DCAF aim to improve?
quiz.answer: It aims to improve the simulation of how single cells respond to genetic perturbations.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, so its findings are preliminary.

items.title: Associated factors for stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis or septic shock: A systematic review.

ai.headline: Stress ulcers and gut bleeding in sepsis are linked to patient, illness and treatment factors, not one single cause.
ai.summary: A systematic review of six observational studies involving 131,568 adults with sepsis or septic shock found that stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding affected between 2.0% and 32.3% of patients. Associated factors included older age, previous gut bleeding, liver disease, cancer, kidney problems, shock, mechanical ventilation and certain medicines.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows doctors may need to decide who gets ulcer-preventing treatment based on individual risk rather than giving it to everyone with sepsis.
ai.fact: Stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in sepsis are linked to factors such as shock, kidney problems, liver disease, previous gut bleeding and mechanical ventilation.

quiz.question: What did the review find about the rate of stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding in people with sepsis or septic shock?
quiz.answer: Across six studies, the rate varied between 2.0% and 32.3%.

ai.caveat: The review combined observational studies, which can show links but cannot prove that these factors cause stress ulcers or bleeding.

items.title: The Frequency of Neuropsychiatric Sequelae After Traumatic Brain Injury in the Global South: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: After traumatic brain injury in parts of Asia and Africa, depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, sleep problems and cognitive impairment are common.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at studies from Western Asia, South Asia and Africa on mental health and thinking problems after traumatic brain injury. It found depression in about 35%, anxiety in about 29%, PTSD in about 20%, OCD in about 19%, sleep disturbance in about 27% and cognitive impairment in about 49% of people studied.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that brain injury can be followed by common mental health and thinking difficulties, so people recovering from head injuries may benefit from checking for these issues.
ai.life_skill: Notice changes in mood, sleep or thinking after a head injury and mention them to a healthcare professional.
ai.fact: Cognitive impairment was the most frequently reported problem after traumatic brain injury in the regions studied.

quiz.question: Which problem was most common after traumatic brain injury in this review?
quiz.answer: Cognitive impairment, found in about 49% of people studied.

ai.caveat: The studies used different diagnostic tools and measures, so the results are not perfectly consistent.

items.title: Human-Centric Logistics: The Role of Human Resource Management in Building Resilient and Sustainable Supply Chains in Africa: A Systematic Review
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

ai.headline: Investing in people’s skills, wellbeing and engagement makes African supply chains more resilient and sustainable.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 70 studies looked at human resource management in African logistics and supply chains. It found that skills gaps and poor engagement are common, while training, talent management and wellbeing support can strengthen supply chains, though African-specific evidence is limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that the people behind moving goods matter as much as trucks or technology for keeping everyday supplies flowing.
ai.life_skill: Notice how training, support and good working conditions affect the reliability of services you use.
ai.fact: Human capital is described as the keystone of African supply chain performance.

quiz.question: What does the review say is the key and most overlooked factor for resilient and sustainable supply chains in Africa?
quiz.answer: The human aspect—capabilities, motivation, working conditions and engagement.

ai.caveat: The African-specific evidence base is small and scattered, with much of it speculated by replicating international research.

items.title: Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Bipolar Disorder

ai.headline: A new brain-based education approach for bipolar disorder is proposed but not yet tested.
ai.summary: The paper reviews neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE), which teaches people with bipolar disorder about brain circuits, reward processing, body clocks, and nervous system regulation. It suggests this could improve awareness, reduce stigma, help treatment adherence, and build self-efficacy, but says direct evidence for NIPE in bipolar disorder is still limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how learning about the brain might help people manage a long-term mental health condition, though more research is needed.
ai.life_skill: Try learning how sleep and daily routines affect your mood, and discuss any changes with a qualified mental health professional.
ai.fact: Bipolar disorder involves changes in brain circuits, reward processing, body clocks, and nervous system regulation across mood states.

quiz.question: What does the paper say about direct evidence for neuroscience-informed psychoeducation in bipolar disorder?
quiz.answer: It says empirical evaluation of NIPE specifically for bipolar disorder remains limited.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint chapter proposing an approach, not a tested study with results.

items.title: Using archaeometabolomics to characterise tobacco-usage in human cortical bone from 17 th to 19 th century Dutch communities

ai.headline: Chemical analysis of old bones can reveal whether people in the past used tobacco.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed human cortical bone from Dutch communities dating from the 17th to 19th centuries using two mass spectrometry methods. They found distinct chemical profiles that helped distinguish tobacco consumers from non-consumers, including between pre- and post-tobacco periods.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how science can uncover everyday habits from the past even when teeth are missing.
ai.fact: Metabolomic profiles in bone can differ between people who consumed tobacco and those who did not.

quiz.question: What did the researchers use to analyse tobacco use in old bones?
quiz.answer: They used two mass spectrometry methods called RP C18 and HILIC.

ai.caveat: The study shows a link between chemical profiles and tobacco use but cannot prove causation, and the authors say more work is needed to separate other variables.

items.title: Statistical analysis plan for the feasibility trial assessing external trigeminal nerve stimulation versus sham stimulation for ADHD in children and adolescents aged 7 to 17 years (the eTNS4ADHD trial)

ai.headline: Researchers have set out how they will analyse a trial testing nerve stimulation for ADHD in children.
ai.summary: The paper describes the statistical plan for a pilot trial comparing external trigeminal nerve stimulation with sham stimulation in children and adolescents aged 7 to 17 with ADHD. items.title: The Impact of Basketball Training and Competition on Oxidative Balance, Inflammation Intensity, and Muscle Damage – Perspectives for Recovery
items.venue: Journal of Education, Health and Sport

ai.headline: Intense basketball training and games temporarily raise muscle damage, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers.
ai.summary: This review examined how basketball training and competition affect muscle damage, inflammation, and oxidative balance. It found that intense play triggers short-term rises in these markers, which generally settle within 24 to 48 hours. ai.why_it_matters: Knowing that short-term soreness and fatigue are normal after hard exercise helps people plan rest and understand typical recovery symptoms.

ai.fact: Intense exercise temporarily raises markers of muscle damage, inflammation, and oxidative stress, which usually settle within a day or two.

quiz.answer: They generally settle within 24 to 48 hours.

items.title: Intelligent scaffolding for musical practice: a systematic review of AI and digital support for the self-regulated learning cycle.

ai.headline: Digital and AI tools can support independent music practice, but too much help may reduce learner autonomy.
ai.summary: A review of 16 studies examined how digital tools and AI support the planning, performance, and reflection stages of independent music practice. Traditional tools helped with planning and reflection, discriminative AI detected errors in real time, and generative AI could turn expert feedback into practical steps. The authors warn that over-scaffolding may reduce autonomy and that visual feedback might distract learners from sound.
ai.why_it_matters: Knowing how practice apps shape independence can help learners choose technology that supports their own judgement rather than replacing it.
ai.life_skill: Try fading app hints and feedback over time so you keep making your own decisions while practising.
ai.fact: Traditional digital tools support planning and reflection, while discriminative AI can detect errors in real time during practice.

quiz.question: What did traditional digital tools support in the music practice cycle?
quiz.answer: They supported the planning and reflection phases of self-regulated learning.

ai.caveat: The studies were methodologically varied and many were small or cross-sectional, so the review cannot establish causal effects.

items.title: Conceptualizations and measurements of family flourishing and wellbeing: a scoping review

ai.headline: Family flourishing is a new idea with few good ways to measure it yet.
ai.summary: A review of 13 studies examined how family flourishing and wellbeing are defined and measured. It found seven family wellbeing measures but no dedicated family flourishing measures, and most tools are old with limited quality testing.
ai.why_it_matters: This matters because it shows we still lack clear, reliable ways to tell whether a whole family is thriving, not just its individual members.
ai.life_skill: Talk with your family about what helps your household feel connected and purposeful, not just free from problems.
ai.fact: No dedicated measure of family flourishing was found in the studies reviewed.

quiz.question: How many measures of family flourishing did the review find?
quiz.answer: It found none, only seven measures of family wellbeing.

items.title: Climate factors and child health in Sweden: a nationwide whole-population study of 4.6 million school-aged children

ai.headline: Hot days, big daily temperature swings, and rain are linked to more child hospital admissions in Sweden.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 4.6 million Swedish children aged 6–18 using linked national health records. Higher mean temperature, both low and high intraday temperature variability, and higher precipitation were linked to more all-cause hospital admissions. Relative humidity showed no association, and risks were higher among younger children and in East Sweden.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that everyday weather swings and rainy days, not just extreme heatwaves, may affect children's health and should inform public health warnings.
ai.life_skill: Check weather forecasts for extreme heat and large daily temperature swings, especially around younger children.
ai.fact: Hot weather and large swings in temperature within a single day are linked to higher hospitalisation rates among children in Sweden.

quiz.question: Which weather factor showed no link to hospitalisation risk?
quiz.answer: Relative humidity showed no association with hospitalisation risk.

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are preliminary.

items.title: Problematic media use, but not device time, tracks mental health issues: A four-wave cohort study in adolescents

ai.headline: Problematic media use, not just screen time, is linked to adolescent mental health issues.
ai.summary: This preprint followed 550 Swiss adolescents over two years to compare the effects of device time versus problematic use on mental health. It found that while screen time predicted problematic use, only problematic use—especially of social media—was strongly linked to anxiety, depression, and ADHD symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that worrying about how many hours you spend on a device is less useful than noticing if you feel unable to control your usage.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether you feel compelled to check your phone or social media even when you want to stop, rather than just counting your hours.
ai.fact: In this study, problematic social media use showed strong reciprocal ties with mental health issues, whereas screen time was only weakly associated.

quiz.question: According to the study, which factor was more strongly linked to mental health issues: total screen time or problematic use?
quiz.answer: Problematic use, particularly of social media, was more strongly linked to mental health issues than total screen time.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it shows associations rather than proving that problematic use causes mental health problems.

items.title: Crowdstorming You Can Trust? Assessing the Reliability of Crowdsourced Ideation and Prioritization

ai.headline: Different groups of people often come up with similar good ideas when solving the same problem.
ai.summary: Researchers asked two separate groups of MBA students to independently suggest and rank ways to improve their course. They found that both groups proposed semantically similar ideas, especially the valuable ones, and prioritised them in a similar order.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that collective decision-making can be more consistent and reliable than people usually assume, even without everyone talking to each other.
ai.life_skill: Notice that when you ask different friends for advice on the same problem, their best suggestions often overlap.
ai.fact: In this study, two independent groups converged on similar high-quality ideas while diverging on poor ones.

quiz.question: Did the two groups agree more on good ideas or bad ideas?
quiz.answer: The groups showed convergence among valuable ideas and divergence among poor ones.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a single exploratory study with one specific group of students, so it is not yet peer-reviewed proof.

items.title: Personalized and differentially private federated learning for mobility data mining via the TrajectoryGuard framework

ai.headline: A new framework lets devices train mobility models together without sharing raw GPS data, keeping location traces private.
ai.summary: The study tested TrajectoryGuard, a privacy-preserving federated learning system that keeps raw location traces such as GPS logs on users' devices while using differential privacy and secure aggregation to train models. On the GeoLife and T-Drive Beijing taxi datasets, it reached 92.5% accuracy for predicting destination categories and cut communication overhead by 30% per round, with a privacy guarantee of ε = 0.9 at σ² = 1.0.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how cities and apps could analyse movement patterns for transport planning without collecting people's actual location histories.
ai.life_skill: Check an app's privacy settings to see whether it shares your raw location data or only processed insights.
ai.fact: Federated learning trains models across many devices without centralising raw user data.

quiz.question: What did TrajectoryGuard predict from partial GPS trajectories?
quiz.answer: It predicted a destination category such as home, workplace, or shopping location.

ai.caveat: The results come from experiments on specific datasets and a proposed framework, not from real-world deployment across diverse populations.

items.title: Development of Sleep Intervention for Parent and Child

ai.headline: A trial is testing a programme to help parents manage thoughts linked to childhood sleep problems.
ai.summary: The study develops and tests an intervention for parents of children with behavioural insomnia of childhood. It focuses on helping parents manage their thoughts about their child's sleep.
ai.why_it_matters: Sleep problems in children affect many families, and this research looks at how parents' thinking may play a role.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your thoughts about your child's sleep affect your own reactions at bedtime.
ai.fact: Behavioural insomnia of childhood is a recognised sleep condition in children.

quiz.question: Who is the intervention programme designed to help?
quiz.answer: It is designed to help parents manage their thoughts when their child has sleep problems.

ai.caveat: The abstract only states the study's aim and does not report any results or findings yet.

items.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective

ai.headline: AI safety systems can wrongly block harmless questions, and researchers propose a way to reduce this.
ai.summary: The study examines why safety-aligned large language models sometimes refuse harmless queries that look risky. It finds that harmful and over-refused samples become harder to distinguish in deeper model layers, and that harmful-sample gradients are more aligned with refusal targets than helpful targets on over-refusal prompts. The authors propose a framework called GOAL to reduce over-refusal while keeping safety performance.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why AI assistants may refuse safe requests, which matters as more people rely on them for everyday information.
ai.life_skill: If an AI refuses a harmless question, try rephrasing it or check with another source before assuming the topic is unsafe.
ai.fact: Safety-aligned large language models can mistakenly reject harmless queries that appear superficially risky.

quiz.question: What did the study find about harmful and over-refusal samples in deeper model layers?
quiz.answer: Their representations increasingly overlap, making it harder for the model to keep a clear boundary between them.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings should be treated as preliminary.

items.title: Transcranial electrical stimulation for memory enhancement: A systematic review and meta-analysis

ai.headline: Brain stimulation is linked to small memory improvements in healthy adults, but effects are short-lived.
ai.summary: This systematic review analysed 193 trials involving over 7,000 healthy adults to see if transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) improves memory. It found a small overall benefit for working and declarative memory compared to fake stimulation, with effects lasting up to one day.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that non-invasive brain stimulation might be a safe tool for boosting cognitive performance, though the gains are modest and temporary.
ai.life_skill: Notice that while technology can offer small cognitive boosts, consistent practice and sleep remain the most reliable ways to support memory.
ai.fact: Tingling and itching on the scalp were more common during active stimulation than during sham sessions, but no serious adverse events were reported.

quiz.question: How long did the memory improvements from stimulation last in this study?
quiz.answer: Significant pooled effects were observed within 1 day after stimulation, while longer-term estimates were imprecise.

ai.caveat: The study is a preprint not yet peer-reviewed, and the authors note that heterogeneity and small-study effects limit conclusions about long-term safety and durability.

items.title: Negative affectivity moderates the association between job demands and hair cortisol in healthcare workers: a cross-sectional multi-method study

ai.headline: Stress from certain job demands may raise long-term stress hormone levels more in people high in negative affectivity.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 67 healthcare workers in Northern Italy, measuring job demands, negative affectivity, and hair cortisol as a marker of long-term stress. Job demands were not linked to cortisol overall, but among people high in negative affectivity, problem solving and time pressure were more strongly linked to higher hair cortisol.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that personality differences can shape how workplace stress affects the body over time.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether time pressure or problem solving at work affects your stress more than it does for others, and consider discussing workload with a supervisor or occupational health professional.
ai.fact: Hair cortisol concentration is used as a biomarker of long-term activation of the body’s stress response system.

quiz.question: What did the study find about job demands and hair cortisol in people high in negative affectivity?
quiz.answer: Among people high in negative affectivity, problem solving and time pressure were more strongly linked to higher hair cortisol.

ai.caveat: This was a small cross-sectional study of 67 workers, so it cannot show that job demands cause changes in cortisol.

items.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers

ai.headline: A new method speeds up AI video generation by skipping most attention calculations while keeping quality high.
ai.summary: The study tested AB-Attention, a training-free technique that approximates full attention in video diffusion transformers by selectively computing only important blocks of data. On two video models, it skipped 89–92% of attention work, improved image quality by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline, and achieved up to 2.23 times faster end-to-end speedup.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI video tools can become faster and more efficient without losing visual quality, which could make them cheaper and more accessible in everyday use.
ai.life_skill: Try using AI video tools that advertise efficient or accelerated generation to save time and computing power.
ai.fact: AB-Attention can skip 89–92% of attention calculations in video diffusion transformers while maintaining or improving quality.

quiz.question: What did AB-Attention achieve compared to baselines in terms of attention computation?
quiz.answer: It skipped 89–92% of attention, whereas baselines computed 1.8–3.6 times as much.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the findings are based on technical experiments with two specific video models rather than real-world user trials.

items.title: A decade of carbon dioxide data from space gets an upgrade

ai.summary: Two NASA instruments, OCO-2 and OCO-3, take over a million daily observations of sunlight reflecting off Earth. An algorithm uses the physics of light travelling through air to turn these readings into atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.

quiz.answer: They capture sunlight reflecting off Earth's surface, which an algorithm converts into atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations.

items.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms

ai.headline: A weakened brain signal may link several puzzling symptoms of schizophrenia.
ai.summary: Researchers studied brain signals in people with schizophrenia and found that a weakened signal may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity. ai.why_it_matters: It offers a possible explanation for why seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia occur together.
ai.fact: A weakened brain signal may be linked to sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity in schizophrenia.

quiz.question: What did researchers find may connect several symptoms of schizophrenia?
quiz.answer: A weakened brain signal may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity.

items.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan

ai.headline: Two brain architecture gradients map how visual areas are organised and change across life.
ai.summary: Researchers used MRI to study the human visual cortex and found two gradients of cortical structure—one where cell and myelin features converge and another where they diverge. These gradients predict visual brain organisation and new visual representations, and each follows a different pattern across the lifespan.

ai.fact: The visual cortex contains two distinct architectural gradients that relate to visual behaviour and change differently across the lifespan.

quiz.answer: They predicted the structural and functional topography of the visual cortex, including the presence of new visual representations.

items.title: Representation, Innovation, and Product Adoption -- by Jennifer L. Kao, Tamar Oostrom

ai.headline: Paying for elderly people to join drug trials led to more trials and more drug use by older adults.
ai.summary: Researchers studied a 2000 Medicare change that lowered the cost of including elderly people in clinical trials. quiz.answer: Trial sponsors included more elderly participants and ran more trials for diseases common among older people, leading to greater drug use by that group.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the findings come from observing a policy change rather than a randomised experiment.

items.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue

ai.headline: Countries reached a global deal to halt nature decline, but funding remains unresolved.
ai.summary: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track. A deal has been reached at global nature talks. Money remains an issue.

items.title: The Relationship Between Depression and Cognitive Function with the Level of Independence in Daily Living Activities Among Older Adults at Sabai Nan Aluih Sicincin

ai.headline: Depression and poorer thinking skills are linked to less independence in daily activities among nursing-home residents.
ai.summary: The study looked at 80 older adults in one nursing home and measured depression, cognitive function, and independence in daily living activities. It found that both depression and cognitive function were significantly associated with independence levels.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how mental health and thinking skills can affect everyday independence for older adults in care.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether low mood or memory difficulties are making daily tasks harder, and consider mentioning it to a care worker or health professional.
ai.fact: Depression and cognitive function are significantly associated with the level of independence in daily living activities among older adults.

quiz.question: What did the study find about depression and cognitive function in relation to independence?
quiz.answer: Both were significantly associated with the level of independence in daily living activities.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study at one nursing home, so it shows a link but cannot prove cause and effect.

items.title: Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions for reducing dental anxiety and improving behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients: a systematic review with GRADE assessment.

ai.headline: Sensory changes like adapted dental rooms, screens or music may lower children's dental anxiety and improve cooperation, but evidence is only moderate at best.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 47 studies, including 25 randomised or controlled trials, looked at sensory-based approaches such as sensory-adapted dental environments, audiovisual distraction or virtual reality, music therapy, aromatherapy and weighted blankets for children up to 18 years old. The strongest evidence supported sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality, while music therapy had lower certainty; overall certainty ranged from very low to moderate because of bias, varied methods and imprecise results.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that simple, non-drug changes to the dental setting may help anxious children, though more high-quality research is needed before they become routine.
ai.life_skill: If a child feels anxious about dental visits, ask the dental team whether a calmer environment, headphones, music or a video could be used during treatment.
ai.fact: Dental anxiety affects an estimated 9%-20% of children and disproportionately impacts those with neurodevelopmental conditions.

quiz.question: Which sensory-based approaches had the strongest evidence for reducing children's dental anxiety and improving cooperation?
quiz.answer: Sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality had moderate-certainty evidence, the strongest among the approaches reviewed.

ai.caveat: This is a systematic review of trials with overall low-to-moderate certainty, limited by risk of bias, heterogeneity and imprecise results, so it supports cautious use rather than proof of routine benefit.

items.title: Neonatal Sleep Disruption and Brain Development in Preterm Infants: A Narrative Review of Neurodevelopmental Outcomes

ai.headline: Sleep disruption in preterm babies may be linked to later brain and behaviour outcomes, but proof is limited.
ai.summary: The review looked at studies of preterm infants in neonatal intensive care and how noise, light, caregiving and painful procedures can disrupt sleep. ai.fact: Sleep supports brain maturation, synaptic plasticity and white matter development in newborns.

quiz.answer: It is linked to altered brain development, attention problems, attachment difficulties and stress system changes, but causal relationships remain difficult to establish.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review of observational studies and meta-analyses, not a randomised trial, so it cannot prove that sleep disruption causes later problems.

items.title: Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.

items.title: Effect of virtual reality-based exergaming on multidimensional outcomes in individuals with cognitive impairment: a three-level meta-analysis based on the ICF framework

ai.headline: Virtual reality exercise games may improve thinking, movement and quality of life in people with cognitive impairment.

It found possible improvements in memory, attention, executive function, balance, muscle strength, mobility and quality of life, but not in depressive symptoms, overall fitness or fall risk.

quiz.answer: Depressive symptoms, comprehensive physical fitness and fall risk showed no significant effect.

items.title: Problematic internet use among young people in Türkiye: a meta-analysis

ai.headline: Among young people in Türkiye, more time online is strongly linked to higher problematic internet use.
ai.summary: This meta-analysis combined 27 studies of 16,488 high school and university students in Türkiye. It found male students reported slightly higher problematic internet use than female students, those using the internet the most each day reported much higher problematic use than those using it the least, and family income showed no clear link.

ai.fact: The gender gap in problematic internet use among young people in Türkiye was small and appeared to be getting smaller in more recent studies.

quiz.question: Which factor was most strongly linked to problematic internet use in this meta-analysis?
quiz.answer: Students in the longest daily internet-use category reported substantially higher problematic internet use than those in the shortest category.

ai.caveat: All included studies were cross-sectional, so they show associations rather than prove that time online causes problematic internet use.

items.title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly

ai.headline: A review of early research on Apple Vision Pro finds benefits, technical limits, and unresolved ethical concerns.

items.title: Causal Intervention Modeling of Exercise--Sleep--Mental Health for College Students from Multimodal Wearable Data

ai.headline: Researchers built a model to test whether changing exercise could improve sleep and mental health in college students.
ai.summary: The study used wearable data from two student datasets to model how reallocating time to exercise might affect next-night sleep and later mental-health outcomes. ai.why_it_matters: It shows how wearable data could be used to understand whether lifestyle changes might influence wellbeing, rather than just spotting links.
ai.life_skill: Notice how changes in your daily activity relate to your sleep and mood over the following days.
ai.fact: The paper presents a modelling framework for estimating how exercise reallocation may affect sleep and mental health using observational wearable data.

quiz.question: What kind of data did the researchers use to study exercise, sleep and mental health?
quiz.answer: They used multimodal wearable data from two college student datasets.

items.title: AI Incidents and Marginalized Populations: A Descriptive Analysis of the AI Incident Database (1983–2026) from a Social Work Perspective

As age increased, people were more likely to perceive averted gaze as direct, especially for non-fearful expressions, and greater perceived direct gaze was linked to higher trustworthiness ratings, particularly among older adults.
ai.why_it_matters: This may help explain why older adults sometimes place greater trust in others and could be more vulnerable to deception.
ai.life_skill: Notice where someone’s eyes are actually pointing before deciding whether they seem trustworthy.
ai.fact: Direct gaze is generally interpreted as an approach signal, while averted gaze is interpreted as an avoidance signal.

quiz.question: What happened to trustworthiness ratings as perceived direct gaze increased?
quiz.answer: Greater perception of direct gaze was associated with greater facial trustworthiness attributions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the online design cannot prove that age causes these differences in gaze perception or trust judgments.

items.title: Synthetic Reception: Manufacturing the Signals of Uptake in Hype and Technology Expectations

ai.headline: Companies can secretly fake signs that lots of people like a new technology to make it seem popular.
ai.summary: The paper studies how hype is created not just by promises but by how audiences receive them. It introduces “synthetic reception,” where producers hide their own role in creating signals of uptake—such as likes, early reactions or endorsements—so they look like independent audience judgements.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people question whether apparent public excitement about a new app, device or trend is genuine or manufactured.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether excitement about a new technology comes from many independent voices or looks like a coordinated campaign.
ai.fact: Signals of uptake such as counts, first reactions and endorsements shape what audiences decide deserves attention.

quiz.question: What does “synthetic reception” fake?
quiz.answer: It fakes the independence of a signal of uptake, making a producer’s concealed contribution look like independent audience judgement.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and offers a conceptual framework rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma

ai.headline: An AI tool that maps immune cells in lung cancer tissue may predict survival better than current tests.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an AI method called the focal TIL score that measures immune cell density in specific areas of lung cancer tissue using standard pathology images. In a study of 685 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, higher focal TIL scores were linked to longer overall survival and outperformed the standard PD-L1 biomarker.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could make cancer prognosis more objective and standardised using images hospitals already produce.

quiz.question: What did the focal TIL score measure in lung cancer tissue?
quiz.answer: It measured the density of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes within specific tiles across the tissue region.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the survival finding comes from an observational association rather than a randomised trial.

items.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD

ai.headline: Academia can suit early-career academics with ADHD, but institutional pressures often block that potential.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed early-career academics with ADHD about their work experiences. They found that ADHD traits can bring strengths such as curiosity and exploration, but social and institutional pressures often make it harder to thrive. The study argues that both individual careers and collective knowledge production can benefit when universities include and support neurodivergent academics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace context shapes whether neurodivergent traits help or hinder people at work.
ai.life_skill: Notice which work settings help you focus and which create friction, and consider asking for adjustments that suit your needs.
ai.fact: ADHD traits can include both challenges, such as time management, and strengths, such as curiosity-driven exploration.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about academia for early-career academics with ADHD?
quiz.answer: Academia can be rewarding for them, but social and institutional pressures often inhibit that potential.

ai.caveat: This is a small interview-based study, so its findings cannot be generalised to all academics with ADHD or proven to apply universally.

items.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history

ai.headline: Ancient ice found in Tibet
ai.summary: Scientists discovered ancient ice in Tibet that may be over 128,000 years old, preserving a record of Earth's climate. The ice provides a glimpse into the last ice age and could reshape understanding of glacier survival. The discovery reveals new information about Earth's climate history.
ai.why_it_matters: This discovery could change our understanding of how glaciers respond to climate change, impacting everyday life and the environment.
ai.life_skill: Explore how climate change affects your local environment.
ai.fact: Ancient ice in Tibet may be over 128,000 years old.

quiz.question: How old is the ancient ice found in Tibet?
quiz.answer: The ancient ice may be more than 128,000 years old.

ai.caveat: The discovery is reported in a news article and may not have been peer-reviewed, so the findings should be treated with caution.

items.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

ai.headline: One AI model can both rerank search results and generate answers, saving memory and time.
ai.summary: The study tested Glance, a system that lets a single 9-billion-parameter AI model score and rerank retrieved passages using a lightweight adapter instead of running a separate reranking model. On two retrieval datasets it matched or beat a strong reranker, and on 300 HotpotQA questions it improved answer quality by a small but statistically supported margin.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI search tools could become faster and cheaper to run by using one model for several jobs instead of many.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI answer cites its sources before trusting it.
ai.fact: Glance achieved nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, compared with 0.721 and 0.326 for bge-reranker-v2-m3.

quiz.question: What did Glance use to score candidate passages without prefilling each pair separately?
quiz.answer: A lightweight decision adapter and pointer head branching from a shared cached context.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and evaluation covers only two retrieval datasets, one QA dataset and one backbone family.

items.title: Impact Of Early Cognitive Rehabilitation On Functional Outcomes Following Moderate Traumatic Brain Injury

ai.headline: Cognitive rehab aids brain injury recovery
ai.summary: This study examined the impact of early cognitive rehabilitation on patients with moderate traumatic brain injury. The study aimed to detect the effect of this rehabilitation on functional outcomes. The results of the study are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the impact of cognitive rehabilitation can inform treatment approaches for traumatic brain injury patients
ai.life_skill: Try seeking professional help for brain injuries
ai.fact: Cognitive rehabilitation is used to aid recovery from traumatic brain injuries

quiz.question: What type of injury did the study focus on?
quiz.answer: Moderate traumatic brain injury

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not be fully peer-reviewed or published yet

items.title: [Articles] Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
authors: Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz, Michele Kong, Sidharth Mahapatra, Adam J Schwarz, Suwannee Phumeetham, Katherine Irby, Natalie Napolitano, Onella S Dawkins-Henry, Emily E Birch, Corrine F Elliott, Lindsay R Berry, Kevin J Downes, Aruna Natarajan, Michelle A Detry, Kert Viele, Todd L Graves, Michael Matthay, Lisa A Asaro, David Wypij, PROSpect Study Investigators, Paediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators Network

ai.headline: Prone positioning and HFOV not recommended
ai.summary: Researchers studied prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome. They found no evidence to support these strategies as first-line treatments. The study was a randomised controlled trial.
ai.why_it_matters: This finding impacts the treatment of children with acute respiratory distress syndrome, influencing medical decisions and patient care.
ai.fact: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation do not improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome.

quiz.question: What was found regarding prone positioning and HFOV in early PARDS?
quiz.answer: No evidence was found to support their use as first-line strategies.

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not apply to all patients or situations beyond the study's parameters.

items.title: A new neural code for position: generalizable spatial maps in mouse medial frontal cortex

ai.headline: Mouse frontal cortex cells may encode position using distances to landmarks, helping navigation.
ai.summary: Researchers imaged brain cells in mice exploring a square arena with landmarks. Activity in the medial frontal cortex could predict the animal’s position even in areas where the model was not trained, unlike cells in the hippocampus or orbitofrontal cortex. A model based on squared distance to multiple landmarks explained this pattern.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a way the brain might generalise known locations to plan routes through new spaces.
ai.life_skill: Notice landmarks around you to help work out where you are in an unfamiliar place.
ai.fact: Medial frontal cortex activity in mice was linked to spatial position across different parts of an arena.

quiz.question: Which brain region showed position predictions that generalised to a new area of the arena?
quiz.answer: The medial frontal cortex, but not the dorsal hippocampus or lateroventral orbitofrontal cortex.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and was done in mice, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: New travel tool combines three algorithms to tailor destination recommendations

ai.headline: Researchers built a travel tool that uses three algorithms to suggest destinations based on preferences, budgets and routes.
ai.summary: The paper describes a new tourist recommendation system that combines three algorithms to match destinations to travelers’ preferences, budgets and travel routes. It aims to fix a limitation of digital platforms that often prioritise popularity over practical considerations.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how digital tools could help people plan trips that fit their real-life constraints rather than just popular spots.
ai.life_skill: Try comparing travel suggestions against your own budget and route before picking a destination.
ai.fact: Some digital travel platforms tend to prioritise popularity over practical considerations like budget and route.

quiz.question: What does the new travel tool combine to tailor destination recommendations?
quiz.answer: It combines three algorithms to match destinations to preferences, budgets and travel routes.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a paper, not the peer-reviewed study itself, so no methods or results can be verified from the abstract.

items.title: This Arabian desert was once a lush paradise. Why did ancient humans avoid it?

ai.headline: Desert was once lush
ai.summary: An expedition studied an Arabian desert that was once a lush paradise. The team found that water alone was not enough for human settlement. Proposals to block sunlight were also considered.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding why ancient humans avoided this area can provide insights into human migration and settlement patterns.
ai.life_skill: Explore how environmental factors influence human decisions
ai.fact: The Arabian desert was once a lush paradise

quiz.question: What was the Arabian desert like in the past?
quiz.answer: It was once a lush paradise.

ai.caveat: The study's findings are based on a single expedition and may not be conclusive.
